procnotices.bid_description: Operation & Maintenance Services- Management and Affermage Contracts for capacity building, operation and maintenance of Cabinda Provincial Water and Sanitation Utility
procnotices.contact_address: Rua Via S8, Condomínio DOLCE VITA, Edifício A1, 3º andar, Talatona, Luanda, Angola
procnotices.notice_text:
Procurement Notice

 

Notice of Request for Bids

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Request for Bids

Operation & Maintenance Services

 

Operation & Maintenance Services- Management and Affermage Contracts for capacity building, operation and maintenance of Cabinda Provincial Water and Sanitation Utility

 

Employer: The Financial and Contract Management Unit (FCMU-WB/AFD) of the Ministry of Energy and Water (MINEA)

Project: SECOND WATER SECTOR INSTITUTIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSIDP 2)

Contract title: Operation & Maintenance Services - Management and Affermage Contracts for capacity building, operation and maintenance of Cabinda Provincial Water and Sanitation Utility

Country: Angola

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: IBRD-87020/ IBRD-88760/ COFN-C1560

RFB No: 81ANC1/CABINDA/PPP/26

Issued on: July 2nd, 2026

 

1. The Government of the Republic of Angola (GoA) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Second Water Sector Institutional Development Project (WSIDP-2), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments for the Cabinda PPP (as defined in Section II) only for, PHASE 1: MANAGEMENT CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY (Empresa Pública de Águas e Saneamento de Cabinda-EP - EPAS CABINDA). PHASE 2: AFFERMAGE CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY (Empresa Pública de Águas e Saneamento de Cabinda-EP - EPAS CABINDA will be subject to the terms stated in this Procurement Notice and Bid Document. For this contract regarding Phase 1, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

 

2. The procurement forms part of the implementation of the Cabinda PPP, which comprises: PHASE 1: MANAGEMENT CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY AND PHASE 2: AFFERMAGE CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY

 

3. The Financial and Contract Management Unit (FCMU-WB/AFD) of the Ministry of Energy and Water (MINEA) now invites sealed Bids from Bidders for the following contract: PHASE 1: MANAGEMENT CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY (Empresa Pública de Águas e Saneamento de Cabinda-EP - EPAS CABINDA). The Services (as defined in Section II), to be provided under the Management Contract (as defined in Section II) will be for a period of 3 years and the Contractor (as defined in Section II) will ensure that EPAS Cabinda (as  defined in Section II), is managed and operates as a financially independent and technically sustainable entity that is able to meet its service level obligations to Customers as defined under the law, regulations and agreements with the Government.  PHASE 2: AFFERMAGE CONTRACT FOR CAPACITY BUILDING, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CABINDA PROVINCIAL WATER AND SANITATION UTILITY (Empresa Pública de Águas e Saneamento de Cabinda-EP - EPAS CABINDA. On completion of the Services provided by the Contractor in PHASE 1, and upon meeting the prescribed conditions for the transition to proceed, the Services will transition to PHASE 2 where, within the legal framework of an Affermage Contract (as defined in Section II), for a period of 12 years, the Contractor will take over complete and exclusive administration, management and operational control, of the facilities of EPAS Cabinda in respect of its water services. In return, the Contractor will be remunerated for Services rendered under the Management Contract (PHASE 1) and Affermage Contract (PHASE 2) as per the payment terms stipulated in the Contracts.

 

4. The procurement of the Cabinda PPP shall be conducted as a single procurement process Operation & Maintenance Services- Management and Affermage Contracts for capacity building, operation and maintenance of Cabinda Provincial Water and Sanitation Utility, covering both PHASE 1 (Management Contract) and PHASE 2 (Affermage Contract).  Bidders shall, therefore, submit a single Bid covering both phases of the Cabinda PPP. The successful Bidder shall be awarded for the Contract regarding the PHASE 1 – MANAGEMENT CONTRACT. PHASE 2 – AFFERMAGE CONTRACT should be awarded only after successful completion of PHASE 1 and subject to the performance evaluation requirements. The two Contracts together constitute the complete contractual framework for the Cabinda PPP.

 

5. Notwithstanding that Bidders are required to submit Technical and Financial Bids covering both phases of the Cabinda PPP, the present RFB shall result in the award and execution of the Phase 1 – Management Contract only. The Phase 2 – Affermage Contract is not being awarded or executed under this RFB. However, the draft Affermage Contract forms part of the Bidding Documents in order to enable Bidders to prepare comprehensive Technical and Financial Bids for the overall Cabinda PPP.

 

Subject to:

 

(a) satisfactory performance by the Contractor under the Phase 1 Management Contract, including achievement of all Transitional Conditions;

(b) fulfilment of all Conditions Precedent set out in the applicable PPP legal and contractual framework;

(c) approvals required under the applicable Angolan legal framework (including the Public Contracts Law, the Public–Private Partnership framework and the approval requirements of the Tribunal de Contas); and

(d) confirmation by the Employer that the requirements for transition have been fully satisfied,

 

the Government of Angola commits to awarding the Phase 2 – Affermage Contract to the same Contractor through a direct award upon completion of Phase 1. Accordingly Participation in this procurement constitutes acknowledgement by Bidders that:

  • Phase 1 and Phase 2 form part of a single Cabinda PPP;
  • the present RFB awards only the Phase 1 Management Contract; and
  • award of the Phase 2 Affermage Contract remains conditional upon satisfaction of the contractual, legal and regulatory requirements governing the transition from Phase 1 to Phase2.

 

6. Bidding will be conducted through a single-stage two envelope Request for Bids (RFB) process in accordance with an international competitive procurement process as specified in the World Bank’s “Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025, Sixth Edition (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

 

7. The procurement shall utilize Rated Criteria, a Technical Threshold, and a Most Advantageous Bid evaluation methodology as specified in the Bidding Document (as defined in Section II). The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 70 % and for Bid cost: 30%.

 

8. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Financial and Contract Management Unit (FCMU-WB/AFD) of the Ministry of Energy and Water (MINEA), Attention: Ms. Elsa Ramos, Project Director, E-mail: pdisa@pdisa.ao and inspect the Bidding Document during office hours Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 hours, Luanda Local time at the address given below.

 

9. The Bidding Document in English may be obtained free of charge by prospective eligible Bidders, upon the submission of a written application to the address below. The Bidding Document will be sent by email in a non-editable format. If delivery by courier is requested, the cost shall be borne by the interested eligible Bidder.

 

10. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 10:00 Angola Local Time October 22nd, 2026. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PROPOSAL” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below, at October 22nd, 2026 at 10:00 Angola Local Time. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PROPOSAL” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.

 

11. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security in the form of a on first demand, autonomous and unconditional Bank Guarantee in the amount and currency of one hundred fifty thousand US Dollar only (USD 150,000.00) or equivalent in local currency or any freely convertible currency.

 

12. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Notification of Award, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the Bidding Document.

Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire.

L'Unité de Gestion du Projet RIZ PLUS sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la fourniture, la livraison et l'installation de 1 105 kits de matériels FLID (kits d'irrigation solaire) destinés à la Région Sofia, constituant un lot unique et indivisible, répartis comme suit :

  • 225 Kits « Imersol » (pompe solaire immergée, 2 panneaux de 380 W minimum)
  • 135 Kits « Fixasol » (pompe solaire sur support fixe, 3 panneaux de 435 W minimum)

Les lieux de destination finale, au sens de la version des Incoterms spécifiée dans le Dossier d'appel d'offres, sont constitués par les sites d'implantation des kits, situés dans les sept (07) districts de Mampikony, Port-Bergé, Analalava, Antsohihy, Bealanana, Befandriana-Nord et Mandritsara, Région Sofia, République de Madagascar. Les Fournitures transitent par un magasin de transit à Antananarivo puis par les chefs-lieux de district, conformément au calendrier de livraison figurant dans le Dossier d'appel d’offres.

Les prestations comprennent, outre la fourniture des équipements conformes aux Spécifications techniques de la Section VII : le transport jusqu'au magasin de transit d'Antananarivo, l'ensemble des formalités et frais d'importation et de dédouanement, le magasinage, le gardiennage et l'assurance des Fournitures au magasin de transit, l'allotissement par district et la réexpédition jusqu'aux chefs-lieux des sept districts, le transport terminal jusqu'aux sites d'implantation, l'installation et la mise en service de chaque kit avec essais de bon fonctionnement, la formation individuelle de chacun des 1 105 exploitants bénéficiaires sur sa parcelle, une démonstration collective par district, la fourniture de la documentation technique en langue française, la remise d'un rapport final d'exécution par district, la disponibilité des pièces de rechange et d'un point de service après-vente dans chacun des sept districts d'installation, ainsi qu'une garantie de vingt-quatre (24) mois à compter de la réception provisoire prononcée par district.

Les délais contractuels sont les suivants :

a) Fourniture et livraison de l'intégralité des 1 105 kits au magasin de transit d'Antananarivo : cent cinq (105) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de notification de l'ordre de service de commencer ;

b) Allotissement par district, réexpédition et livraison de l'intégralité des kits aux chefs-lieux des sept (07) districts de la Région Sofia : soixante (60) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de réception quantitative des Fournitures au magasin de transit ;

c) Services connexes comprenant le transport terminal jusqu'aux sites d'implantation, l'installation, la mise en service, les essais de bon fonctionnement et la formation des exploitants de l'ensemble des kits : cent quatre-vingts (180) jours calendaires au plus tard, comptés à partir du lendemain de la date de notification de l'ordre de service d'installation. Cet ordre de service est émis par l'Acheteur après achèvement de la livraison aux chefs-lieux de district, et au plus tôt le 1er avril 2027, la période d'installation devant coïncider avec le calendrier cultural des exploitants bénéficiaires.

Les frais de magasinage, de gardiennage, d'assurance et de réexpédition entre les délais a) et b) sont à la charge exclusive du Fournisseur et réputés inclus dans le prix de l'Offre. Les lieux de destination finale, demeurent constitués par les sites d'implantation situés dans les sept districts.

Toute offre proposant un délai supérieur à l'un ou l'autre de ces délais sera considérée comme non conforme et écartée. Aucun bonus ne sera accordé pour une exécution anticipée.

Aucune marge de préférence n'est applicable.

República de Guatemala

Programa de Infraestructura Rural y Movilidad para el Buen Vivir

Sector Transporte

ANUNCIO GENERAL DE ADQUISICIONES

Préstamo No. 9847-GT BIRF

ID del Proyecto No. P178573

 

La República de Guatemala, a través del Ministerio de Comunicaciones, Infraestructura y Vivienda -CIV- a través de la Dirección General de Caminos -DGC-, ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento       -BIRF- / Banco Mundial por un monto equivalente a US$400 millones de Dólares de los Estados Unidos de América, aprobado por el Directorio Ejecutivo del BIRF el 30 de junio de 2025 y ratificado mediante el Decreto del Congreso de la República número 25-2025 de fecha 25 de noviembre de 2025, para sufragar el costo del Programa de Infraestructura Rural y Movilidad para el Buen Vivir, y tiene la intención de destinar parte de los fondos para efectuar pagos correspondientes a la adquisición de Bienes, Obras, Servicios de No-consultoría y Servicios de Consultoría que se contraten en el marco de este Programa.

El objetivo de desarrollo del Programa es mejorar la conectividad vial resiliente al clima y fortalecer la gestión del sector vial nacional. El Programa tiene una duración estimada de implementación de siete (7) años, interviniendo caminos rurales, carreteras departamentales y nacionales, priorizando aquellas zonas con mayor vulnerabilidad al cambio climático y necesidad de acceso, además se proporcionarán herramientas y métodos para la gestión de activos viales y estrategia de mantenimiento eficiente, contribuyendo así a una red de transporte más sostenible y funcional. El área de intervención del Programa está en 14 departamentos del país, distribuidos en las siguientes regiones prioritarias: (i) El Altiplano: Huehuetenango, San Marcos, Quiché, Totonicapán, Quetzaltenango, Sololá y Chimaltenango; (ii) Las Verapaces: Alta Verapaz y Baja Verapaz; y (iii) El Corredor Seco: El Progreso, Zacapa, Chiquimula, Jalapa y Jutiapa.

 

El Programa consta de los siguientes componentes:

Componente 1: Caminos Rurales, y Carreteras Departamentales y Nacionales (costo estimado: US$384 millones). Este componente financiará los bienes, los servicios de consultoría, los servicios no relacionados con la consultoría, las obras civiles para la rehabilitación y mejoramiento de caminos rurales y carreteras en las regiones de interés a través de tres subcomponentes:

•    Subcomponente 1.1 – Reposición y mejoramiento de caminos rurales (US$215.3 millones): Garantizar la transitabilidad durante todo el año, incluyendo mejoras al sistema de drenaje, estabilización de taludes, pavimentación, construcción de puentes, alcantarillas e infraestructura para peatones y transporte no motorizado, con enfoque de resiliencia climática y seguridad vial.

•    Subcomponente 1.2 – Reposición y mejoramiento de carreteras departamentales y nacionales (US$162.7 millones): Mejoramiento y pavimentación resiliente de carreteras departamentales y nacionales para la conectividad municipal y rural en zonas de alto riesgo climático.

•    Subcomponente 1.3 – Fortalecimiento de la capacidad de respuesta ante emergencias de las Zonas Viales (US$6 millones): Adquisición de maquinaria para las Zonas Viales de las áreas seleccionadas para respuesta ante fenómenos meteorológicos extremos.

Componente 2: Gestión Estratégica del Sector Vial (costo estimado: US$5 millones).

Este componente apoya el fortalecimiento institucional de la DGC y el CIV, y financiará la contratación de los siguientes servicios de consultoría:

 

  1. Metodología de priorización y selección de las intervenciones del Proyecto;
  2. Manual de diseño de caminos rurales resilientes al clima, seguros e inclusivos;
  3. Gestión de activos viales: revisión y fortalecimiento del mantenimiento de la red vial rural, y desarrollo y uso de herramientas digitales para mejorar la gestión de los caminos rurales;
  4. Análisis de brechas e implementación de un plan de acción para desarrollar las condiciones habilitantes para la movilización de capital privado para el sector vial;
  5. Promoción de equidad de género en el sector vial: Diseño e implementación de un plan de acción para la Unidad de Género del CIV, y Programa de formación certificada para mujeres en la construcción y/o el mantenimiento de caminos;
  6. Implementación de una hoja de ruta de las mejores prácticas internacionales en temas ambientales, sociales y de gobernanza.

 

Componente 3: Gestión del Proyecto. (costo estimado: US$11 millones).

Este componente financia los costos operativos de la Unidad Coordinadora del Programa (UCP), y las contrataciones de los servicios de consultoría, servicios no relacionados con la consultoría y bienes, así como los costos de administración, monitoreo y evaluación del programa.

Los contratos financiados por el Préstamo se llevarán a cabo a través de los procedimientos especificados en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones del Banco Mundial para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión: Adquisiciones en Operaciones de Financiamiento para Proyectos de Inversión – Bienes, Obras, Servicios de No Consultoría y Servicios de Consultoría (Edición), publicada en febrero de 2025 y con entrada en vigor el 1 de marzo de 2025 (las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones  para prestatarios FPI), y están abiertos a todas las empresas y personas elegibles según se define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones. El Banco Mundial dispondrá la publicación en su sitio web externo del plan de adquisiciones inicial acordado y de todas las actualizaciones subsiguientes una vez que haya otorgado una no objeción.

Los avisos específicos de contratación correspondientes a los procesos sujetos a convocatoria pública internacional abierta se anunciarán, a medida que estén disponibles, en el sitio web externo del Banco Mundial (https://www.worldbank.org), en el portal electrónico del Sistema de Información de Contrataciones y Adquisiciones del Estado –GUATECOMPRAS– (https://www.guatecompras.gt), en el Diario de Centro América (https://legal.dca.gob.gt), así como en medios impresos o digitales de amplia circulación, y otros medios que se consideren apropiados para promover la participación del mercado internacional.

Se requerirá Precalificación para los contratos de obras civiles; y para los contratos de consultoría se requerirá Expresión de Interés, según sea acordado entre la DGC y el Banco Mundial.

Las empresas y personas interesadas que reúnan los requisitos y deseen ser consideradas para la provisión de obras, bienes, servicios no relacionados con la consultoría y servicios de consultoría para el Programa mencionado anteriormente, o aquellas que requieran información adicional, deben ponerse en contacto con el Prestatario en la siguiente dirección:

procnotices.bid_description: Consulting Services for the Development of an Institutional Strengthening Strategy, Roadmap, and Action Plan for Sustainable Agricultural Land Management in Georgia
procnotices.contact_address: 34 Marshal Gelovani Avenue, Tbilisi 0159, Georgia
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

GEORGIA

Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL) – P175629

Loan No. 9504-GE 

Assignment title: Consulting Services for the Development of an Institutional Strengthening Strategy, Roadmap, and Action Plan for Sustainable Agricultural Land Management in Georgia

 

Reference No. GR/CS/CQS/15

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land (GRAIL) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The project cost is USD 150.00 million comprising of an equal share of USD 75.00 million by each co-financer.

The project development objectives are to: (a) improve irrigation, and drainage services, and agricultural production in project areas; and (b) strengthen national irrigation and land management institutional capacity for climate resilient planning. The primary project beneficiaries comprise farmers and agricultural enterprises across the project targeted regions. Overall, the rural population will benefit from enhanced services provided by land management, irrigation services, and agricultural support. In the public sector, the project will support institutional strengthening of Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture (MEPA), including Georgian Amelioration (GA), Rural Development Agency (RDA) and Land Management Agency (LMA). The Project consists of the following two main components: Component 1. Resilient Irrigated Agriculture and Component 2: Improved Land Management Capacity.

To ensure the long-term sustainability of agricultural resources, the Government seeks to strengthen the institutional framework and develop a clear roadmap supporting sustainable land management (SLM). Therefore, this assignment is designed to provide the technical assistance necessary to assess existing capacities and establish a robust Institutional Strategy and Action Plan for the LMA and relevant MEPA departments, specifically the Hydro-melioration and Land Management Department (MLMD) of MEPA.

The overarching goal of the assignment is to guide the strategic, technical, and institutional empowerment of the LMA and the MLMD of MEPA, ensuring they can effectively execute their statutory responsibilities through modern, data-driven frameworks. The primary objective of the Institutional Strengthening Strategy and the accompanying 5-year strategic roadmap is to provide MEPA and the LMA with a comprehensive, evidence-based blueprint for institutional modernization. Rather than dictating immediate technical execution, these strategic deliverables will be designed to logically sequence necessary administrative reforms, optimize business processes and align with statutory land management mandates, establish the conceptual prerequisites for future digital transformation, and define a clear, costed path for long-term operational and financial sustainability. Rather than redefining mandates already set by their statutes, the Strategy and Action Plan will structure and phase interventions across four core components:

  • Institutional Strategy: Defining what the entities do, how they are optimally structured, and how they are financially sustained;
  • Business Processes: Mapping and reengineering how they operate internally and exchange data with external registries and agencies;
  • Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) Strategy & Enterprise Architecture: Defining the specific technology architecture, readiness parameters, and priority use cases that enable those business processes;
  • Data Architecture: Modeling conceptual target data environments, metadata rules or instructions, and operational data flows;

 

Key objectives include:

  • land management to identify specific gaps and opportunities for technical and administrative reform, and to translate existing legal mandates into clear, efficient technical workflows and administrative business processes for both entities;
  • Develop targeted recommendations and proposals to support the harmonization of land-related legislation with broader environmental and agricultural policies, aimed at fostering a coherent legal framework for sustainable land use;
  • Conduct a comprehensive capacity assessment and develop a Strategy for the Institutional Development of the LMA and relevant MEPA structures (specifically the MLMD), focused on strengthening their ability to fulfill statutory responsibilities that will include the proposed optimized organizational setups, human resource strategies, and staffing models tailored to support modernized workflows of the entities;
  • Formulate Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and explicit operational plans for specialized land management mandates. This includes: (i) the planning, restoration, rehabilitation, and landscape-level cultivation of windbreaks; (ii) the national pasture inventory program and sustainable management practices; and (iii) monitoring, supervision, and regulatory compliance workflows for topsoil preservation and management - all in accordance with existing legislation and the forthcoming Law on Sustainable Pasture Management;
  • Explore Advanced Land Monitoring and Remote Sensing Feasibility: Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the practical operational requirements, data readiness, technical infrastructure constraints, and user needs to conceptually integrate modernized LCLU monitoring and automated crop identification use cases leveraging satellite data (e.g., Sentinel) and relevant geoprocessing tasks into daily workflows, and detail integration into the strategic roadmap. This shall include a rigorous evaluation of international standards (such as FAO, EU INSPIRE, or IPCC) and relevant country best practices to define, justify, and adapt the technical and methodological frameworks required to institutionalize continuous, evidence-based land monitoring tailored to Georgian operational requirements;
  • Develop a comprehensive 5-year public finance model to support recurring expenses for IT infrastructure, system asset maintenance, data procurement pipelines, and technical staff development across both entities;
  • Provide a comprehensive capacity building framework, including a detailed training-of-trainers (ToT) curriculum and technical user guides, ensuring that staff within the LMA and MLMD possess the internal capacity required to manage the strategy and roadmap independently.

Indicative assignment duration: The duration of the assignment is estimated at twelve (12) months from the date of contract signature.

The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of interest should cover, but not limited to: corporate profile, years in business, experience relevant to the project activities, overall key staff resources, and core business.

The selection criteria are:

The Consultant shall be a firm/consortium with demonstrated experience in:

  • Institutional Expertise: A minimum of 10 years of experience in institutional reform, land management policy, and public sector governance, including the development of national-level land management strategies and action plans;
  • Specialized SLM Expertise: Proven track record and a multidisciplinary pool of specialists with documented expertise across the key thematic areas of Sustainable Land Management (SLM) as relevant to the scope and objectives of this assignment;
  • Business Process & Conceptual Systems Architecture Capability: Documented corporate experience in large-scale Business Process Reengineering (BPR), conceptual data modeling, and systems integration planning within public administration or land sectors;
  • Digital and Technical Proficiency: Advanced expertise in the conceptual design of Remote Sensing (RS) solutions and LCLU monitoring frameworks, including verified experience in system requirements gathering, technical feasibility assessments, and conceptual design of targeted machine learning use cases;
  • Proven experience in assessing and designing integrated geospatial systems, database management architectures, and business intelligence solutions at institutional or national scale. (Note: MEPA/LMA use ArcGIS, Microsoft SQL for LCLU inventory and database administration and Microsoft BI for reporting);
  • Capacity Building and Training: A successful track record in designing and executing large-scale public sector capacity development programs, specialized training-of-trainers (ToT) modules, and technical knowledge transfer;
  • Global and Local Context: Previous experience with World Bank, EU, or UN-funded projects is highly desirable. Familiarity with the land management and administration context in Georgia or the South Caucasus region is considered a significant advantage. 

Note: the MEPA reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The experience of sub-consultants will not be taken into account while evaluating the corporate experience of the consultant.

Experience in the projects relevant to the assignment should be submitted in the Form N1 uploaded at: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NaYoSd_zCVJUr3AXewqbaM_a9eLff2FU/view?usp=drive_link       

ToR for the assignment can be found at the following link:  

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GRW_sVmgJTniUGzGtxgI8KP1Nr9dNmAR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111094613369888933218&rtpof=true&sd=true

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations:  Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers - July 2016, September 2025

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 a.m. to 17:00 p.m. at MEPA, Mr. Ioseb Tchonkadze, Procurement Consultant.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in English in written form to the email addresses below by September 08, 2026, at 17:00 (Georgian local time) - extended deadline.

REQUEST FOR CURRICULA VITAE

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

 

COUNTRY: ROMANIA

STRENGTHENING FOUNDATIONS FOR IMPROVED JUSTICE SERVICE DELIVERY PROJECT

Loan No. 9549-RO

Assignment Title: Social Specialist

Reference No. CSI-1-3-2

 

The Government of Romania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Justice Services Improvement Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) main objective is to ensure compliance with national and World Bank’s environmental and social standards in carrying out civil works and other activities (1 Individual Consultant).

The estimated duration of the assignment is until December 31, 2030 (project closing date). The estimated total budget is approx. 108,812 EURO. The contract might be extended or not according to MoJ management decision, depending on MoJ needs and consultant’s performance. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for CV.

The Ministry of Justice - Department for Implementation of Externally Financed Projects (DIEFP) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services as below:

Qualifications and skills – 20 points:

  • University studies in a relevant area (psychology/sociology/other social sciences), completed with a master's degree;
  • PhD degree in a relevant area is highly preferred;
  • Knowledge of relevant national legislation relating to ES matters and the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards;
  • Excellent writing skills, ability to prepare clear and attainable reports;
  • Strong facilitation skills, ability to conduct discussions and to respond to various feedback/questions;
  • Good command of both Romanian and English languages;
  • Computer literate in Microsoft Office (Word and Excel).

General Professional experience – 20 points:

  • at least five (5) years of professional experience in assignments related to social assessment;

Specific Professional experience – 60 points:

  • Demonstrated experience in working with World Bank Environmental and Social Standards;
  • Demonstrated experience for supporting, advising and/or collaborating with public institutions on environmental and social standards / sustainable development etc.;
  • Practical experience in the field of monitoring and evaluation;
  • Experience with international organizations is highly preferred.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

In order to be able to charge the Client for the activities performed under these terms of reference, the expert must be a person authorized under the Law 300/2004 regarding the authorization of individual persons and family associations to carry out independent activities.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: 0900 to 1700 hours, local time.

Expressions of interest and CVs, in English language and/or Romanian language, must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) September 17, 2026, 17:00 local time. To validate the information presented in the CV, the candidate will attach all the relevant supporting documents (studies diploma(s), recommendations, training diplomas, certifications, authorizations etc.).

DRAFT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY:                                MONGOLIA

NAME OF PROJECT:              GOBI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (P514972)

GFPP GRANT NO.:                   TF0D0692

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP FEASIBILITY STUDIES FOR MONGOLIAN CIVIL AVIATION SECTOR AND MURUN (4C AERODROME CODE) AIRPORT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REFERENCE NO.

(AS PER PROCUREMENT PLAN):              ZTYA/20260804058

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Global Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) toward the cost of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project under Grant No. TF0D0692 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  

The consulting services (“the Services”) include two distinct but complementary components.

Component A will establish the analytical and strategic foundations for aviation sector development in Mongolia. It will include a comprehensive aviation sector diagnostic, a proportionate first-pass review of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) safety and security compliance issues relevant to airport network planning and investment readiness, preparation of the Mongolia Airport Network Development Strategy to 2040, a companion Policy Recommendations Note, and a structured stakeholder consultation process. Together, these outputs will provide Government with a practical framework for airport classification, demand development, institutional strengthening, climate resilience, high-level investment prioritization, and identification of follow-on policy and technical assistance needs.

Component B will prepare a full feasibility study for Murun Airport. The Government has identified Murun Airport as a priority project requiring detailed assessment and project preparation. The feasibility study shall evaluate the technical, operational, environmental, social, financial, economic, fiscal, and institutional viability of the proposed investment and define an appropriate development concept for implementation.

The assignment is expected to run for approximately 6 to 7 months from the date of contract effectiveness. Component A and Component B shall proceed in parallel throughout the assignment period.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:

Tender.gov.mn

The Ministry of Road and Transport now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General experience:

General experience implementing consultancy services in the field of civil aviation and transport sector strategy, planning and the feasibility studies; and preliminary/detailed engineering design of projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration, during the last 10 years;

 

 

In addition, demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving the preparation of environmental and social safeguard instruments for World Bank-financed projects or projects financed by comparable multilateral development banks, including at a minimum one of the following: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (P-ESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). Evidence should be provided in the firm`s EoI.

  1. Specific Experiences: 
  1. Proven experience in preparing civil aviation sector development strategies and/or airport feasibility studies (including associated policy, institutional, or PPP/commercial advisory) during the last 10 years. At least 2 such similar contracts should be demonstrated, each with a contract value of not less than US$300,000 (Please be sure to include the contract value in your submission).
  2. The consulting team must include Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.
  1. Technical and managerial organization of the firm

General description of the firm's technical and managerial organization, including the structure of the organization, general qualifications of staff, and number of permanent professional staff. Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The Shortlist will contain up to 6 firms. Shortlisted firms will be issued the full Request for Proposals, which will specify detailed technical and financial evaluation criteria and weightings, including key expert evaluation.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, seventh edition dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: from 09.00 to 17.00 hours (GMT+8).  

The assignment will be carried out in compliance with the World Bank`s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines. ESF competency will be assessed during the subsequent Request for Proposals (RFP) stage as part of the technical evaluation.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20 – Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist)

 

UKRAINE

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project 

Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA

 

Assignment Title: Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

 

Reference No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MOES) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter referred to as Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The Project aims to increase efficiency and improve conditions to ensure quality and transparency in the higher education system of Ukraine.

The purpose of the Consultant's activities is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services

(Individual Consultant)

Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

Procurement No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project

World Bank Loan No. 9238-UA


 

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (hereinafter referred to as "IBRD" or the "World Bank") signed Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA in the amount of US$200 million to implement the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter, the "Project"). The Project is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with support from the World Bank Group.

Project implementation period: 2021-2027.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the efficiency, conditions for quality, and transparency in Ukraine's higher education system.

The Project comprises six components:

  • Component 1: Sector-Wide Improvements to Governance, Financing, Quality and Transparency.
  • Component 2: Alliances and Partnerships for Improved Efficiency and Quality.
  • Component 3: Capacity Building and Education Environment Enhancement.
  • Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation.
  • Component 5: Support to Academic and Social Scholarships for Higher Education Students.
  • Component 6: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).

The Project will finance two expenditure categories: Category (i) - investments in goods, works, and services, with disbursements made against eligible expenditures; and Category (ii) - transfers to the budget upon fulfilment of certain results-based conditions, with disbursements likewise made against eligible expenditures subject to the achievement of specified results, as set forth in the Loan Agreement and the Project Operations Manual.

Within Part 3 of the Project, specialized consultants are planned to be engaged to support the effective management of the higher education and research system, as well as higher education institutions, and to provide support for the implementation of digital, financial, human resources, and other components of higher education reform at the institutional level.

More detailed information about the Project is available at: https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P171050

These Terms of Reference set out the objective and scope of the consulting services, as well as the qualification requirements for the Consultant.

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant's scope of services shall include, but not be limited to:

  • ensure effective working interaction among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, consultants of UIHERP and other stakeholder;
  • collect and consolidate information required for UIHERP implementation;
  • organize the day-to-day work of specialists and consultants of the MoES UIHERP support team;
  • coordinate work-related matters, deadlines, and task priorities;
  • maintain working calendars and records of tasks, deadlines, status, and agreements; send reminders to responsible persons and provide timely notice of delays or the need for management decisions;
  • coordinate the preparation and conduct of working sessions, meetings, events, and visits under the Project; record agreements and monitor follow-up actions;
  • ensure the timely exchange of information among MoES management, structural units, the support consultant team, higher education institutions, partners, and UIHERP;
  • collect, verify for completeness, systematize, and technically format working materials, background information, draft letters, and meeting materials;
  • organize the clearance of documents and materials, track their routing and status, and monitor the completion of assigned tasks;
  • organize the collection of reports from engaged Support Team specialists for the preparation of monthly and other reports required under the Project, and perform other Project implementation tasks within the Consultant's competence;
  • perform other Project-related tasks within the Consultant's competence, as assigned by the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system.

The following outputs and results are expected from the services (the list is not exhaustive):

  • the day-to-day work of MoES specialists, consultants of the higher education support team, and UIHERP is organized;
  • working calendars, task lists, deadlines, status, and agreements are kept up to date; decisions and follow-up actions are recorded and tracked;
  • working meetings, sessions, events, and visits are organized in a timely manner; the necessary materials are prepared and information exchange among the parties involved is ensured;
  • working materials and evidence of task completion are systematized;
  • effective working interaction is ensured among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, the support team and UIHERP, higher education institutions, and other higher education stakeholders;
  • the day-to-day work of the team's specialists and consultants is organized.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator, be accountable to the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system, and work under their supervision.

The Consultant shall coordinate their activities with the Project Manager - Head of the Consultant Team and ensure the administrative coordination of specialists and consultants engaged in implementing UIHERP tasks in higher education.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports in hard copy to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator.

Each monthly report shall include a concise description of the administrative and coordination tasks performed, meetings and events organized, assignments and work processes supported, the status of interaction with engaged specialists, and the materials collected and systematized for UIHERP implementation and reporting. Where necessary, the report shall include agendas, minutes, links, task lists, or other evidence of performance.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES shall provide the Consultant in a timely manner with the information necessary to perform the assignment.

MoES may provide the Consultant with a workspace, including the equipment necessary to perform the functions (e.g., a personal computer, communications equipment, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • a Master's degree or higher;
  • at least three years of professional experience in administrative coordination, project administration, or organizational support for managers or teams in the education sector;
  • experience organizing the work of a team or group of consultants while concurrently managing multiple tasks, deadlines, and clearances;
  • experience preparing working meetings and events, taking minutes or recording agreements, and monitoring their implementation;
  • experience organizing document workflows, clearance processes, and working interaction among structural units, partners, or contractors;
  • skills in collecting, systematizing, and consolidating information for working and reporting materials;
  • strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work with confidential information, manage multiple tasks, and meet tight deadlines;
  • fluency in Ukrainian;
  • English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or higher;
  • proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, videoconferencing platforms, and digital tools for task management and teamwork.

The following preferred (non-mandatory) qualifications, competencies, and experience will be considered an advantage:

  • an academic background in management, public administration, project management, international relations, political science, or a related field;
  • experience in higher education;
  • experience in the public sector;
  • experience providing administrative support to projects financed by international financial institutions or international technical assistance programs;
  • knowledge of other foreign languages will be considered an advantage.

MoES may invite the most qualified candidates for an interview to clarify information provided in their CVs.

VII. PERIOD AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide the services until 30 June 2027. with the possibility of extending the contract if UIHERP is extended.

The Consultant shall provide the services under this Contract on an ongoing basis throughout its term, with a level of effort equivalent to full-time engagement, to the extent necessary for the proper performance of the tasks specified in these Terms of Reference.

The Client and the Consultant may at any time agree on a different workload based on the actual volume of tasks.

Specific contractual terms and working arrangements shall be discussed and agreed separately.

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, marina.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20: [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

ANUNCIO ESPECIFICO DE ADQUISICIONES

CONVOCATORIA

1. El Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado de la Provincial del Guayas (GADP-G)  (denominado en adelante “el Prestatario”) ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para solventar el costo del PROYECTO DE VÍAS RURALES RESILIENTES financiado con fondos y/o recursos del PRÉSTAMO BIRF No. 9722-EC”.

 

2. El Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado de la Provincial del Guayas, invita a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar Cotización sellada para la “CONTRATACIÓN DEL SERVICIO DE INTERNET SATELITAL MÓVIL PARA LA UEP-BM”, conforme los términos establecidos que constan más adelante.

 

3. El proceso se llevará a cabo por medio de una adquisición competitiva con enfoque nacional en la que se utilice el método de Solicitud de Cotizaciones (SDC), conforme lo previsto en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, Séptima Edición de Septiembre de 2025, y se encuentra abierta a todos los Licitantes elegibles, según se define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

 

4. Se solicita que presente una cotización para todos los servicios que se listan en esta invitación.   Las cotizaciones de precios serán evaluadas teniendo en cuenta las condiciones requeridas, sin adjudicaciones parciales; se adjudicará la contratación a la firma que ofrezca el costo más bajo, siempre que cumpla sustancialmente con las especificaciones y requerimientos detallados en la Solicitud de Cotización. 5. Sus cotizaciones deberán estar acompañadas de la documentación técnica adecuada y de cualquier otro material que sea pertinente a la cotización de los servicios.

 

6. Las cotizaciones deberán estar de acuerdo con los Términos y Condiciones para los servicios solicitados, conforme está descrito en esta Solicitud de Cotización.

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA - INDIVIDUAL)

País:                            Moçambique

Nome do Projecto:     Estradas Resilientes ao Clima para o Norte (CRRN - P500488)

Concessão Nº:            E315-MZ

Título do Serviço:      Serviços de Consultoria de um Especialista em Gestão de Riscos de Segurança

Número de Ref.:        47A003041/CP/43/2026

Cliente:                      Administração Nacional de Estradas, Instituto Publico (ANE, IP)

 

1. O Governo de Moçambique (GdM) recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear as Estradas Resilientes ao Clima para o Norte (CRRN) e pretende aplicar parte das receitas para o pagamento dos Serviços de Consultoria de um Especialista em Gestão de Riscos de Segurança, doravante designados como “Serviços”.

2. O principal objectivo do/a Especialista em Gestão de Riscos de Segurança é de assegurar a implementação actualização do Plano de Gestão de Segurança (PGS) do Projecto CRRN, garantindo a protecção de pessoas, bens, activos e infraestruturas, bem como a continuidade operacional das actividades do projecto.

3. Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para o serviço podem ser obtidos no seguinte link https://www.fe.gov.mz/storage/app/uploads/public/6a8/44d/d9b/6a844dd9b1325844730998.pdf ou alternativamente no endereço abaixo.

4. A Administração Nacional de Estradas, IP convida os Consultores Individuais elegíveis ("Consultores") a manifestar o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços durante dois (2) meses a tempo inteiro estará baseado em Maputo, com deslocações, se necessário, aos locais abrangidos pelo projecto nas províncias de Cabo Delgado, Nampula e Niassa.

5. Os Consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante para executar os Serviços.

6. A avaliação das manifestações de interesse será feita numa base qualitativa de acordo com uma matriz robusta de pontos fortes e fracos e a lista curta será composta a partir da lista de consultores individuais qualificados considerando os seguintes critérios:

  • Licenciatura em Gestão de Segurança, Gestão de Riscos, Estudos de Segurança, Justiça Penal, Direito, ou área relacionada;
  • Formação especializada em Gestão de Riscos (ISO 31000 será uma vantagem);
  • Possuir certificações internacionais (é uma vantagem);
  • Mínimo de 10 (Dez) anos de experiência profissional relevante;
  • Experiência em gestão de segurança de infraestruturas;
  • Experiência comprovada em gestão de segurança em áreas afectadas por conflito ou elevado risco operacional será uma vantagem;
  • Experiência em coordenação com forças públicas;
  • Conhecimento da legislação moçambicana em matéria de segurança;
  • Experiência em projectos financiados por instituições internacionais (vantagem);
  • Excelentes capacidades de liderança, análise, comunicação e gestão de crises;
  • Domínio do Português e Inglês (obrigatório).

7. Chama-se a atenção aos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos, 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 dos “Regulamentos de Contratação para Mutuários da IPF” do Banco Mundial de Setembro de 2025 (“Regulamentos de Contratação”), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

8. O consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método do consultor individual (IC) previsto nos Regulamentos de Contratação.

9. Mais informações podem ser obtidas no endereço abaixo durante o horário normal de expediente, das 07:30 às 15:30 horas (hora local), de segunda a sexta-feira, excepto feriados:

procnotices.notice_text:
CONSELHO MUNICIPAL

PROJECTO DE TRANSFORMAÇÃO URBANA DE MAPUTO

Project ID No.: P171449

 

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

(Servicos de Consultoria – Selecção de Firmas)

Elaboração do Plano de Estrutura Urbana do Municipio de Maputo

 

Projecto:             Projecto de Transformação Urbana de Maputo

Project ID:          171449

Activitade:          Elaboração do Plano de Estrutura Urbana do Municipio de Maputo 

Refª.:                    MZ-CMM-490872-CS-QBS  

 

O Governo de Moçambique recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para o Projecto de Transformação Urbana de Maputo, implementado pelo Conselho Municipal de Maputo, e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para custear as despesas de serviços de consultoria para proceder à Elaboração do Plano de Estrutura Urbana do Município de Maputo (PEUMM), em conformidade com a Lei n.º 19/2007, de 18 de Julho (Lei de Ordenamento do Território) e o respectivo Regulamento, aprovado pelo Decreto n.º 23/2008, de 1 de Julho, com vista a materializar a visão estratégica de desenvolvimento territorial do Município face às transformações urbanas, demográficas, económicas, sociais, ambientais e institucionais ocorridas desde a aprovação do 1.º PEUMM em 2008.

 

Objectivo da Consultoria

A elaboração do PEUMM deverá dotar o Conselho Municipal de Maputo de um instrumento estratégico de ordenamento territorial, operacional e orientado para a implementação, capaz de orientar o crescimento urbano sustentável, promover a utilização eficiente do solo, reforçar a integração entre uso do solo, mobilidade e infra-estruturas, aumentar a resiliência urbana às alterações climáticas e apoiar a programação e coordenação dos investimentos públicos e privados.

Sem prejuízo de outros objectivos que decorram do desenvolvimento da consultoria, a elaboração do novo PEUMM deverá: (i) avaliar o grau de implementação do PEUMM (2008), identificando os principais avanços, constrangimentos, oportunidades e lições aprendidas, com vista ao fortalecimento da sua eficácia enquanto instrumento estratégico de ordenamento territorial; (ii) Elaborar o diagnóstico territorial, urbano, socioeconómico, ambiental, institucional e de mobilidade do Município de Maputo, incorporando as dinâmicas de crescimento urbano, as tendências demográficas, as alterações climáticas, os riscos naturais, a evolução do quadro legal e institucional e os investimentos estruturantes realizados ou em curso; (iii) Elaborar o modelo territorial do Município, definindo a estrutura espacial, o sistema de centralidades, a organização do uso e ocupação do solo, a estrutura ecológica, a rede de infra-estruturas e equipamentos, os corredores de mobilidade e as áreas prioritárias de desenvolvimento, regeneração, densificação, expansão e protecção ambiental; (iv) Assegurar a integração entre o ordenamento do território, o sistema de mobilidade urbana, em particular o Sistema MOVE/BRT, e os demais investimentos estruturantes, promovendo uma ocupação do solo orientada para o transporte público e uma utilização mais eficiente das infra-estruturas urbanas; (v) Definir uma estratégia territorial integrada que promova o desenvolvimento urbano sustentável, a inclusão social, a competitividade económica, a valorização do património natural e cultural, a adaptação às alterações climáticas, a redução do risco de desastres e o reforço da resiliência urbana; (vi) Harmonizar o PEUMM com o quadro legal e regulamentar em vigor, os Instrumentos de Ordenamento Territorial, as políticas públicas, os planos sectoriais e os programas e projectos estratégicos com incidência no território municipal, assegurando a sua coerência e complementaridade; (vii) Estabelecer orientações e directrizes para a elaboração, revisão e implementação dos Instrumentos de Ordenamento Territorial de nível inferior, promovendo uma gestão territorial integrada, articulada e coerente em todo o Município; (viii) Definir prioridades territoriais de investimento, mecanismos de implementação, monitoria, avaliação e revisão do Plano, incluindo um programa de acção faseado, indicadores de desempenho e um quadro institucional que assegure a efectiva operacionalização do PEUMM; (v) Promover um processo de planeamento participativo e inclusivo, envolvendo as instituições públicas, o sector privado, a academia, as organizações da sociedade civil e as comunidades locais, de forma a reforçar a apropriação institucional e social do Plano e a sua exequibilidade, conforme recomendado pela legislação aplicável e pelo PTUM (PEPI, QGAS, QPR e PCAS); (ix) Identificar áreas com potencial impacto de deslocamento físico e/ou económico, propondo princípios orientadores para a sua gestão em fases subsequentes de implementação, em conformidade com o QPR.

Os Termos de Referência (TDR) detalhados para a tarefa, bem como informações adicionais, podem ser obtidos enviando uma solicitação para o e-mail fornecido abaixo.

Perfil do Consultor

O Consultor deverá ser uma pessoa colectiva (empresa de Consultoria) legalmente constituída, com experiência comprovada na prestação de serviços de consultoria em ordenamento do território e planeamento urbano. E com capacidade de mobilizar e garantir a permanência de uma equipa multidisciplinar durante o período afecto à elaboração do plano. A empresa deve demonstrar capacidade para trabalhar em Moçambique, conhecimento do contexto institucional e legal, bem como capacidade para integrar as seguintes áreas: urbanismo e ordenamento do território, mobilidade urbana, infraestruturas urbanas, ambiente, componente social, economia urbana e Sistemas de Informação Geográfica (SIG). Deverá ainda ter disponibilidade de ferramentas e metodologias para análise territorial e espacial (SIG), modelação urbana, planeamento participativo e avaliação ambiental e social.

A empresa deverá estar inscrita no Ministério que superintende a área de Ordenamento Territorial.

 

Os critérios de pré-selecção

(i) mínimo 10 (dez) anos de experiência em ordenamento do território e planeamento urbano, sobretudo na elaboração de instrumentos de ordenamento do território e estratégicos de nível municipal, que tenham sido aprovados e submetidos a ratificação; (ii) Mais deve ter experiência comprovada em países em desenvolvimento, preferencialmente na África Subsaariana e a experiência em Moçambique, será considerada uma vantagem; (iii) Deverá ainda ter experiência em projectos financiados por doadores internacionais; (iv) Participação, nos ultimos 10 (dez) anos, em pelo menos 3 (três) projectos semelhantes, ou seja: elaboração de instrumentos de ordenamento do território de nível municipal, que cubram toda a área municipal e projectos que envolveram a integração de propostas de uso de solo, mobilidade e infraestruturas (água, saneamento, drenagem); (v) Experiência em: i) regularização fundiária (será considerada uma vantagem experiência em assentamentos informais), ii) planeamento participativo (consultas públicas), iii) integração de alterações climáticas e resiliência urbana e iv) desenvolvimento de planos de investimento urbano: (vi). Os principais especialistas não serão avaliados na fase de pré-selecção.

O Conselho Municipal de Maputo convida empresas de consultoria elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse na prestação dos Serviços. Os Consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem possuir as qualificações necessárias e a experiência relevante para a execução dos Serviços.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários do IPF” do Banco Mundial, 6ª Edição, fevereiro de 2025, que estabelece a Política do Banco Mundial sobre Conflito de Interesses.

Os consultores podem associar-se a outras empresas para aprimorar suas qualificações e devem indicar claramente se a associação se dá na forma de uma joint venture ou de uma subconsultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os membros da joint venture serão solidariamente responsáveis por todo o contrato, se selecionados.

Um consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método de Seleção Baseada em Qualidade (QBS) estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

As Manifestações de Interesse, incluindo os documentos comprobatórios, devem ser entregues por e-mail para o endereço fornecido abaixo, até 16 de Sertembro de 2026.

CONVOCATORIA

1. El Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado de la Provincial del Guayas (GADP-G)  (denominado en adelante “el Prestatario”) ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para solventar el costo del PROYECTO DE VÍAS RURALES RESILIENTES financiado con fondos y/o recursos del PRÉSTAMO BIRF No. 9722-EC”.

 

2. El Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado de la Provincial del Guayas, invita a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar Cotización sellada para la “CONTRATACIÓN DE PÓLIZAS DE SEGURO DE VIDA Y ASISTENCIA MÉDICA DERIVADA DE ACCIDENTES O SINIESTROS PARA EL PERSONAL DE LA UNIDAD EJECUTORA DEL PROYECTO BM-P504400 (UEPBM-P504400)”, conforme los términos establecidos que constan más adelante.

Su Cotización deberá ser presentada de acuerdo con las instrucciones indicadas en la Sección 1 a continuación, y deberá ser dirigida a la dirección abajo señalada.

 

5. Sus cotizaciones deberán estar acompañadas de la documentación técnica adecuada y de cualquier otro material que sea pertinente a la cotización de los servicios.

 

6. Las cotizaciones deberán estar de acuerdo con los Términos y Condiciones para los servicios solicitados, conforme está descrito en esta Solicitud de Cotización.

 

7. El periodo de entrega de los servicios detallados anteriormente es conforme el siguiente detalle:

 

-El plazo de cobertura inicia a partir de la suscripción del contrato; y,

-La vigencia de las pólizas será de setecientos treinta (730) días contados a partir de la fecha de activación de estas.

 

8. Todas las Cotizaciones deben ir acompañadas de una Declaración de Mantenimiento de Oferta, según el formato que consta en la Solicitud de Cotización.

 

9. Si un Oferente retira su Cotización durante el periodo de validez y/o no acepta la adjudicación del contrato, éste será excluido de la lista de Oferentes del proyecto por un periodo de dos años, según lo establecido en la declaración de mantenimiento de la oferta.

Las cotizaciones recibidas fuera del plazo establecido serán rechazadas.

 

El sobre exterior de la Oferta marcados como “OFERTA ORIGINAL” y los sobres interiores marcados como “PARTE TÉCNICA” y “PARTE FINANCIERA” se abrirán públicamente en presencia de los representantes designados por los Licitantes y cualquier persona que decida asistir, en la dirección que figura a continuación:  Luque 406 y Pichincha, Edificio Banco Park, piso 14, Sala de reuniones de la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto del Banco Mundial, la apertura pública de las cotizaciones.

MINISTERIO DE PRODUCCIÓN SOSTENIBLE, MEDIO AMBIENTE Y AGUA

PROGRAMA DE GESTION RESILIENTE DEL AGUA PARA

RIEGO COMUNITARIO Y FAMILIAR

P178861 - CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO N° 9643-BO

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

Organismo Ejecutor:

Ministerio de Producción Sostenible, Medio Ambiente y Agua, a través de la Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP – PPCR)

Dirección:

Oficinas de la UCP - PPCR, calle Fernando Guachalla, Edificio Nicole N° 2186 entre Ecuador y Sánchez Lima, Zona Sopocachi de la ciudad de La Paz

País:

Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia

Nombre del Proyecto:

Proyecto de Gestión Resiliente del Agua para Riego Comunitario y Familiar P178861 - CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO N° 9643-BO

Servicios a Contratar:

SERVICIO FORTALECIMIENTO ORGANIZACIONAL Y ASISTENCIA TÉCNICA PRODUCTIVA (FORATP) PAQUETE 2: “CONSTRUCCIÓN SISTEMA DE MICRORIEGO ALTA TICANOMA (SACACA) y MEJORAMIENTO SISTEMA DE RIEGO TECNIFICADO HUALLCA (SANTIAGO DE HUARI)”

Período comprendido de los Servicios:

El servicio de Consultoría tendrá una duración de (900 dc), a partir de la fecha de la ORDEN DE INICIO DEL SERVICIO DE CONSULTORÍA

Fuente de Financiamiento:

Banco Mundial – BIRF- 9643-BO

Código del Proceso - STEP:

BO-UCPR-PPCR-569578-CS-CQS

Fecha de publicación de la SEI:

27 de agosto de 2026

Fecha límite de recepción de Expresión de Interés:

11 de septiembre de 2026, hasta horas 15:30 p.m

Esta Invitación Incluye:

Anexo I - Términos de Referencia

Anexo II – Conflicto de Interés

Anexo III - Fraude y Corrupción

Estimados señores:

1. El Programa de GESTION RESILIENTE DEL AGUA PARA RIEGO COMUNITARIO Y FAMILIAR a través del P178861 - CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO N° 9643-BO, tiene como objetivo la gestión integrada de recursos hídricos con enfoque de cuenca e incrementar la resiliencia ante la variabilidad climática de familias rurales vulnerables en microcuencas seleccionados. Sus objetivos específicos son: i) Apoyar a las familias más vulnerables en el acceso a agua para riego y el uso eficiente del recurso hídrico como respuesta al déficit hídrico, a través de la implementación de sistemas de riego menor y el fortalecimiento de la gestión y organización, para contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria. ii) Contribuir a asegurar la disponibilidad de agua para la conservación y recuperación de cuencas, a través de proyectos de manejo integral de cuencas (forestación, manejo de praderas nativas, vigiñas de infiltración, etc.) en cuencas con alta demanda hídrica y con riesgos de escasez hídrica, iii) Proteger las áreas productivas vulnerables a través de proyectos de gestión de riesgos (barreras vivas acompañadas de obras de encauzamiento, muros de hormigón ciclópeo y hormigón, diques longitudinales, etc.) que regulen, conduzcan y minimicen los impactos producidos por las inundaciones, torrenteras y crecidas,  iv) Promover una nueva Cultura del Agua para la Vida en el área de intervención del Programa, a través de acciones de formación, capacitación y sensibilización en niños, jóvenes, productores, regantes, técnicos y profesionales de los Gobiernos Autónomos Municipales (GAM) y Gobiernos Autónomos Departamentales (GAD), y otros actores de la cuenca, que contribuya a garantizar la sostenibilidad de las inversiones, v). Fortalecer la gobernanza local para la gestión y manejo sostenible del agua en las cuencas de intervención del programa, a través de la planificación hídrica estratégica y la elaboración de estudios de inversión que den respuesta a las demandas y necesidades en las cuencas.

2. El Ministerio de Producción Sostenible, Medio Ambiente y Agua, a través de la Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP – PPCR), le invita a presentar Expresión de Interés para el servicio de consultoría (en adelante, los “Servicios”), para la ejecución del FORTALECIMIENTO ORGANIZACIONAL Y ASISTENCIA TÉCNICA PRODUCTIVA (FORATP) PAQUETE 2: “CONSTRUCCIÓN SISTEMA DE MICRORIEGO ALTA TICANOMA (SACACA) y MEJORAMIENTO SISTEMA DE RIEGO TECNIFICADO HUALLCA (SANTIAGO DE HUARI)”

3. Los Términos de Referencia y los Formularios de presentación  para la consultoría se pueden solicitar al correo electrónico ppcr.contrataciones3@gmail.com  o descargar de la página del SICOES https://www.sicoes.gob.bo/portal/index.php, registrado con número de CUCE 26-0041-27-1684209-1-1

4. El Ministerio de Producción Sostenible, Medio Ambiente y Agua, a través de la Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP – PPCR), invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles e interesadas (en delante "Consultores") a manifestar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios.

5. En el caso de firmas que tengan la intención de conformar una APCA (Asociaciones en Participación Asociación en Participación, Consorcio o Asociación), deberán presentar su carta de intención de conformación que indique los porcentajes de participación de cada firma asociada e identifique a la firma líder.

6.Los criterios a ser valorados para la conformación de la Lista Corta son los siguientes:

  1. Fotocopia NIT y SEPREC o documento equivalente para consultoras extranjeras
  2. Identificación de la Firma (a ser presentado en el Formulario (DOC-1).
  3. Experiencia específica: acreditar experiencia de los últimos 10 años, de los cuales deberá contar con un mínimo de 3 (tres) contratos similares relacionados con la consultoría (*). Cada contrato debe haberse realizado por un plazo igual o mayor a 6 meses, los cuales deberán estar declarados en el Formulario DOC-2, adjuntando fotocopias simples que respalden los servicios de consultoría declarados.

(*) las consultorías relacionadas son:

3.1 Servicios de Acompañamiento y/o Asistencia técnica de proyectos de Riego Tecnificado

3.2 Servicios de Acompañamiento y/o Asistencia técnica de proyectos de Riego y/o cuenca

3.3 Servicios de Supervisión de Acompañamiento y/o Asistencia técnica en riego tecnificado, riego y/o cuenca

3.4 Servicios de Supervisión en proyectos de inversión en riego

(**) Según la tipología de proyecto de la presente expresión de interés, se valorará preferentemente la experiencia de las mismas características.

7. Las Firmas Consultoras interesadas deberán adjuntar a su manifestación a Expresión de Interés, los Formularios DOC-1 y DOC-2 debidamente completado, así como la documentación de respaldo presentada en la Expresión de Interés.

8. La Propuesta Técnica (Lógica del Enfoque Técnico, Metodología, Plan de Trabajo, Expertos Clave) y Propuesta Financiera no serán evaluados en la etapa de expresión de interés.

9. La expresión de interés de los consultores interesados es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.11 de la Sección VII de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión, del Banco Mundial Quinta Edición septiembre de 2023 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”). De igual forma, se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”, que establecen la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflicto de interés.

10. Se seleccionará una Firma Consultora de acuerdo con el método de Selección de Calificación de Consultores (SCC) descrito en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones. En esta primera etapa, únicamente se evaluará la capacidad legal y la experiencia relevante de la firma (Formularios DOC-1 y DOC-2).

11. Las consultas y solicitudes de aclaración al presente llamado a Expresiones de Interés podrán realizarlo por medio escrito hasta cuatro (4) días calendario después del presente llamado, mismas que serán atendidas hasta nueve (9) días calendario antes de la fecha límite de manifestación a Expresiones de Interés y comunicadas a través del SICOES en el CUCE correspondiente.

12. Las Expresiones de Interés deberán ser entregadas en formato físico y digital (personalmente o Courier), hasta horas 15:30 p.m. (hora local) de fecha 11 de septiembre de 2026 en la siguiente dirección:

Oficinas de la UCP - PPCR, ubicada en la calle Fernando Guachalla, Edificio Nicole N° 2186 entre Ecuador y Sánchez Lima, Zona Sopocachi de la ciudad de La Paz. El Programa no se responsabilizará por Expresiones de Interés que lleguen con posterioridad a la fecha y hora indicada; asimismo no se devolverá la documentación.

13. Esta Invitación Incluye los Formularios DOC 1 y DOC 2, Anexo I - Términos de Referencia, Anexo II - Conflicto de Interés y Anexo III - Fraude y Corrupción

La Paz, 27 de agosto de 2026.
