Federal Government of Somalia

Ministry of Finance

Invitation for Proposals (IFP)

Design, Supply, Configuration, Integration, Testing, Commissioning, Operationalization and Initial Support of the Somalia National Single Window (NSW) Core Platform, Access Layer, Electronic Payment Layer and Priority System Integrations

Purchaser: Ministry of Finance, Federal Government of Somalia

Project:  De-Risking, Inclusion and Value Enhancement of Pastoral Economies in The Horn Of Africa (DRIVE)

Contract title: Design, Supply, Configuration, Integration, Testing, Commissioning, Operationalization and Initial Support of the Somalia National Single Window (NSW) Core Platform, Access Layer, Electronic Payment Layer and Priority System Integrations

Country: The Federal Republic of Somalia 

Bid Type: Single Stage Bidding – Two Envelope with Rated Criteria

RFP No: SO-MOF-542947-NC-RFP

The Federal Government of Somalia has received grant financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Project DRIVE and it intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payment under the contract for Design, Supply, Configuration, Integration, Testing, Commissioning, Operationalization and Initial Support of the Somalia National Single Window (NSW) Core Platform, Access Layer, Electronic Payment Layer and Priority System Integrations. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments, which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.

The Ministry of Finance of Somalia now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for Design, Supply, Configuration, Integration, Testing, Commissioning, Operationalization and Initial Support of the Somalia National Single Window (NSW) Core Platform, Access Layer, Electronic Payment Layer and Priority System Integrations

The procurement process will be conducted through international competitive procurement with Rated Criteria using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations that meet the following minimum qualification criteria

Proposer’s Financial Capability

  1. The Proposer shall furnish documentary evidence that it meets the following financial requirement(s): the average Annual Turnover in the last three years 2023, 2024 and 2025 to be not less than USD 2,000,000 (Two Million United States Dollars).  

Proposer’s Experience and Technical Capacity

  1. The Proposer should have should have successfully completed at least 1 (One) contract for the implementation of a similar trade facilitation System in the last 5 years in the public or private sector; contract worth more than 2,000,000 USD; submit the completion letter/ contract.
  2. Experience in Developing Countries or Similar Contexts: Proposer should demonstrate experience working in low-resource environments or developing countries with limited infrastructure.
  3. The Proposer must provide at least three (3) Client References for similar successfully completed contracts. At least one of the three references shall be the qualifying contract. Details should include the detailed tasks done, country, year, and Client contact details. Evidence of work done should be supported with Completion Certificates or Reference Letters and value of those contracts

 

  1. Proposer’s Legal Requirements.

The Proposer shall be legally registered entity in its country of origin.

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

 

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

COUNTRY                  : GHANA

NAME OF PROJECT:  SECONDARY EDUCATION TRANSFORMATION FOR ACCESS,   RELEVANCE AND RESULTS FOR JOBS (STARR-J)

 

SECTOR                      : EDUCATION

Credit No                      : IDA - 80670

Project ID No.              : P514793

The Government of Ghana has received a loan of USD 300 million from the World Bank toward the cost of financing the SECONDARY EDUCATION TRANSFORMATION FOR ACCESS, RELEVANCE AND RESULTS FOR JOBS PROJECT to expand access to, and improve the quality and relevance of secondary education in Ghana. The project activities are organized under three interrelated components: Component 1 expands and rehabilitates physical infrastructure to eliminate the double-track system and extend equitable access; Component 2 strengthens teaching quality, TVET relevance, and the availability of learning resources to improve outcomes and labor market alignment; and Component 3 builds the data systems, school leadership capacity, and accountability mechanisms that consolidate access gains and embed quality improvements in system behaviour - ensuring that the project's investments are sustained beyond the project period. 

Key procurement activities per Component are shown below:

S/No.

Activity Description

Component 1: Increase equitable access to Secondary Education

1

Construction of 10 new Senior High Schools (SHS) and Technical and Vocational Institutions (TVI)

2

Upgrade of 50 SHS/TVIs

3

Rehabilitation of 150 SHS/TVIs

4

Procurement of Furniture for SHS and TVIs

5

Procurement of Science Laboratory / Workshop Equipment and Consumables for SHS and TVIs

6

Consultancy Services for Works

Component 2: Improve the quality and relevance of programs in SHS/TVIs

7

Procurement of Textbooks for SHS/TVIs

8

Digitization of Textbooks and other Learning Materials for upload to I-Box/Digital Tools

Component 3: Strengthen systems, communications, and evidence-based decision-making

9

Procurement of Consultancy Services (Firms and Individuals)

10

Strengthening of Data Systems (EMIS upgrade, operation, maintenance, and integration with school mapping)

Procurement under the project will be carried out in accordance with the World Bank "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" (Procurement Regulations), 7th Edition, dated September 2025, and the "Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants", dated July 1, 2016, as well as other provisions stipulated in the Financing Agreement and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided no objection.

Specific procurement notices on contracts for bidding under the World Bank’s Competitive Bidding procedures as they become available on the World Bank external website; Public Procurement Authority Website; and publication in the National Newspapers of wide circulation.

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

***************

 

Nom du pays :

REPUBLIQUE CENTRAFRICAINE

Nom du projet :

PROJET DU CORRIDOR ÉCONOMIQUE DOUALA-BANGUI (PCE)

N° identification :

P 513683

Financement :

BANQUE MONDIALE

N° du Don IDA :

-

Intitulé de la mission :

Recrutement des Experts de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PCE

N° de référence du STEP :

PCE – 23/SC/IND/26 ; PCE – 24/SC/IND/26 ; PCE – 25/SC/IND/26.

 

  1. La République Centrafricaine a obtenu un Don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour couvrir le coût du Projet du Corridor Economique DOUALA-BANGUI (PCE). L’objectif fondamental de ce programme est d’optimiser l’efficacité des transports et la sécurité routière, tout en transformant durablement le quotidien des communautés riveraines au Cameroun et en RCA. Les impacts économiques attendus sont majeurs, ciblant une baisse des coûts logistiques, un meilleur accès aux marchés et une réduction du prix des denrées et du carburant au profit du pouvoir d’achat des ménages.  

                                                                                                                   

  1. Concernant les activités à mettre en œuvre, il s’agira de : (i) Réhabilitation de l’infrastructure du corridor avec amélioration de la sécurité routière, (ii) Amélioration de l’entretien des routes, (iii) Soutien au développement économique inclusif le long du corridor, (iv) Facilitation des transports et du commerce, renforcement institutionnel et gestion de projet, (v) Composante d’intervention d’urgence.

Le projet se concentre sur le corridor Douala-Bangui qui est un axe vital pour le commerce régional, la sécurité alimentaire et la stabilité économique de l'Afrique Centrale. S'étendant sur plus de 1 400 km, dont environ 802 km au Cameroun, il achemine 80 % du commercer extérieur de la République centrafricaine (RCA) et garantit l'approvisionnement alimentaire, la disponibilité en carburant, l'accès humanitaire et la connectivité des marchés. La RCA, économie fragile et fortement dépendante de son territoire, est essentiellement tributaire de ce corridor pour son accès maritime, ce qui en fait avant tout une voie d'approvisionnement et de résilience stratégique, plutôt qu'un corridor économique pleinement développé.

 

  1. Pour la République Centrafricaine, le Projet est élaboré, le corridor relie les zones agricoles fertiles de l'Est du Cameroun et de l'Ouest de la RCA, productrices de maïs, de riz, de cacao, d'huile de palme et d'élevage, aux marchés, tout en traversant des régions riches en minéraux et en forêts, recelant des ressources en or, en diamants et en bois.

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Centrafricaine a donc l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources du Don pour financer les services des Consultants individuels aux différents postes suivants pour assurer la gestion du Projet du Corridor Economique DOUALA – BANGUI.

 

  1. Les postes de recrutement mis en concurrence sont les suivants :
  • Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés, Réf. : PCE – 23/SC/IND/26 ;
  • Responsable Administratif(ve) et Financier(ère), Réf. : PCE – 24/SC/IND/26 ;
  • Comptable, Réf. : PCE – 24/SC/IND/26.

 

  1. Les tâches exhaustives des Experts sont décrites dans les Termes de Référence de chaque mission et sont à retirer au Secrétariat de la Coordination des Projets PURIC-CA, PRACAC et PCE situé au Ministère de l’Equipement et des Travaux Publics à l’adresse indiquée au point 12 ou envoyer par courrier électronique à la demande des candidats intéressés.

 

  1. La Coordination des Projets invite les candidats (consultants individuels) intéressés à manifester leur intérêt pour les postes décrits ci-dessus.

 

  1. Les Consultants intéressés par chaque poste doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services demandés. Le dossier de candidature comprendra les éléments essentiels suivants :
  • Une lettre de motivation précisant le poste et l’adresse du Candidat (téléphone, Email) ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé, certifié, mis à jour, avec trois (3) références professionnelles à contacter, les copies légalisées des diplômes et attestation de travail datant de moins de trois (3) mois.

 

Les Experts seront recrutés sur la base de leurs qualifications académiques, de leurs expériences professionnelles pertinentes et de leur capacité à réaliser la mission. Les numéros de téléphones valides des écoles/universités fréquentées ainsi que des Employeurs passés et actuels devront être ajoutés au CV.

 

Les étapes du recrutement sont les suivants : (i) comparaison des dossiers de candidature et (ii) entretien/interview. La Coordination se réserve le droit de vérifier l’ensemble des informations fournies par les candidats lors de la procédure de sélection.

 

  1. L est porté à l’attention du Consultant que les dispositions du paragraphe 7.32 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale », 7ème édition de Septembre 2025 relatives au recrutement du personnel d’appui à la mise en œuvre des Projets sont applicables. La participation des Fonctionnaires est sujette à l’application des dispositions du paragraphe 3.23 dudit Règlement.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné par poste selon la méthode de comparaison des CV telle que décrite dans le Règlement de « Passation des marchés dans le cadre du financement des Projets de Développement « Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants » du 1er Septembre 2025 accessible sur le site Web de la Banque Mondiale sur http: //www.worldbank.org/procurement en cliquant sur « New Policy and Regulations »

 

  1. Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir les Termes de Référence de chaque mission à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures des bureaux de 9 heures à 15 heures à compter de la date de publication du présent avis.

 

  1. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées par porteur sous pli cacheté en trois (3) exemplaires ou envoyer par courrier express au plus tard le Lundi 21 Septembre 2026 à 13 heures, heure locale à l’adresse suivante :

procnotices.project_name: Kandadji Project
procnotices.bid_description: Travaux de réhabilitation des aménagements hydro-agricoles de Firgoune (Département d’Ayorou)
procnotices.contact_organization: 1ère Partie de la Seconde Phase DREDGE (APL2A) - KANDADJI
procnotices.notice_text:
1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet Kandadji et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché des travaux de réhabilitation des aménagements hydro-agricoles de Firgoune (Département d’Ayorou, région de Tillabéri).

2.  L’Agence du Barrage de Kandadji (ABK) invite, par la présente, les soumissionnaires à présenter leurs Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation de  travaux de réhabilitation des périmètres de Firgoune Nord et Firgoune Sud (curage et recalibrage des chenaux d’amenée et des bâches d’aspiration, remise en état des stations de pompage, réalisation de station de drainage de Firgoune Sud, travaux confortatifs de 4 digues de protection sur 13.450 ml, des canaux primaires sur 2.842 m, secondaires sur 7.300 ml et tertiaires sur 14.236 ml, travaux confortatifs du réseau de drainage 13.577 ml et de pistes 15.335 ml). Le délai d’exécution est 10 mois hors saison des pluies.

 

3.  La procédure sera conduite par Appel d’Offres National (AON) en utilisant une Demande d’Offre tel que défini dans les « Règlement des Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de FPI. » 7ème édition de septembre 2025, est ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles.

 

    4.  Les Soumissionnaires éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de l’Agence du Barrage de Kandadji (ABK) et examiner le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau de 9 :00 à 13 : 00 heures et 15 :30 à 17 : 00 heures à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

5.  Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire éligible en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de deux cent mille (200 000) F CFA. La méthode de paiement sera par versement au compte BOA Niger n° 0601374 0006/73 contre récépissé. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par la poste aérienne pour l’étranger.

 

 

6.  Les Soumissions doivent être remises au Bureau d’ordre de l’Agence du Barrage de Kandadji (ABK), au plus tard le mardi 13 Octobre 2026 à 09 h 30 mn Heure locale (GMT+1). La remise des soumissions par voie électronique ne sera pas permise. Toute Soumission reçue après l’expiration du délai limite de remise des offres sera écartée.

 

     Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des plis le mardi 13 Octobre 2026 à 10 h Heure locale (GMT+1) : Salle de réunion de l’Agence du Barrage de Kandadji  , Quartier RYAD, Avenue BAWA JAN GORZO, BP 206, Niamey - Niger Tel (227) 20 73 23 13 Fax : (227) 20 73 21 85, E-mail : Kandadji@intnet.ne.

 

7.  Les Soumissions doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie d’offre, pour un montant de Soixante-dix Millions (70 000 000) de Francs CFA.

 

8.    « Veillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les propriétaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclus dans le dossier d’appel d’offres ».

 

9.   L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

procnotices.bid_description: Equipements des 23 Institutions Sanitaires Construites ou réhabilitées
procnotices.contact_address:

procnotices.notice_text:
Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AA0)

Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures

(Processus à Deux Enveloppes)

Pays             

RÉPUBLIQUE D’HAITI

Projet                    

PROJET DE RENFORCEMENT DES SOINS DE SANTÉ PRIMAIRE DE

LA SURVEILLANCE (PROSYS)

Intitulé du Marché

Acquisition de quatre (4) lots d’équipement pour trente-cinq (35) institutions sanitaires construites ou réhabilitées

Prêt/Crédit/don No

IDA-D4670

Référence Step      

HT-UGP-405791-GO-RFB/HT-UGP-559030-GO-RFB

Emis le             

27février 2026

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République d’Haïti a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet de Renforcement des soins de santé primaires et de la Surveillance (PROSYS), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché d’Acquisition de quatre (4) lots d’équipements pour trente- cinq (35)institutions sanitaires construites ou réhabilitées. Ce marché est attribuable par lot. Les lots sont ainsi répartis :
  • Lot 1 : Equipements de base ;
  • Lot 2 : Matériels et équipements de radiologie ;
  • Lot 3 : Matériels pour clinique dentaire ;
  • Lot 4 : Matériels divers.

 Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement.

  1. Le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (MSPP) via l’Unité de Gestion des Projets (UGP) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour l’acquisition des fournitures ci-dessus mentionnées, à soumettre des offres électroniques via son système d’achat EUNA PROCUREMENT (Bonfire).
  2. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence internationale (AOI) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » - Février 2025 - de la Banque Mondiale», et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles.
  3. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés savoir (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : 80% et pour le coût de l'Offre : 20%
  4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Gestion des Projets du Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (UGP/MSPP), soit par correspondance physique adressée au bureau de l’UGP/MSPP, situé
  5. Le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres, en version française format PDF, est disponible sur le système d’achat électronique de l’UGP/MSPP:EUNA PROCUREMENT (Bonfire – Haiti Ministry of Health – Unité de Gestion des Projets) pour être consulté par tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles intéressés.
  6. Pour accéder au Dossier d’Appel d’Offres, le Soumissionnaire qui n’est pas encore enregistré sur la plateforme EUNA PROCUREMENT (Bonfire) doit le faire, en cliquant sur le lien suivant :https://mspp.bonfirehub.com/portal/?tab=openOpportunities.
  7. Il s’agit d’une procédure en deux (2) enveloppes :
  8. Les formulaires de soumission, en version modifiables, sont disponibles sur le système d’achat pour être téléchargés, remplis et télé versés par le soumissionnaire.
  9. Le système d’achat BONFIRE n’acceptera pas une soumission à l’expiration du délai limite de remise des offres.
  10. La date limite de soumission d’offre est le 20 avril 2026 à 11h Am ( heure d’Haïti).
  11. Les offres seront ouvertes publiquement de manière hybride (au bureau de la Passation des Marchés de l’UGP/MSPP, sis au n° 3, Delmas 81, et sur la plateforme Bonfire) trente minutes (30 mins) après l’heure limite de soumission, soit  le20 avril 2026 à 11h  30 Am présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes connectées à la session de visioconférence.
  12. Tout soumissionnaire ayant déposé une offre recevra, à l’adresse électronique utilisée lors de la création de son compte fournisseur sur le système d’achat, une invitation de la Passation des Marchés de l’UGP/MSPP pour participer en ligne à la séance d’ouverture des offres « PARTIE TECHNIQUE ».
  13. Les offres financières protégées par un mot de passe resteront non ouvertes.
  14. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une garantie d’offre conformément au modèle du dossier.

L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

procnotices.bid_description: Contratacao de consultoria pessoa juridica para mapeamento e definicao de areas prioritarias nos territorios quilombolas Murumuru e Murumurutuba, subsidiando monitoramento participativo da regeneracao vegetal. Santarem/PA.
procnotices.contact_address: Praia de Botafogo, 190 - Rio de Janeiro
procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA

BRASIL – Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima - MMA

Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia - ASL BRASIL 2

Acordo de Doação N.º TF0B6898-BR – Banco Mundial

Número de Referência: BR-FGV-561336-CS-CQS

DE-ASL2-POA3-SEMAS-2026-0001

 

 

Escopo: Seleção e contratação de consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) especializada em mapeamento e definição de áreas prioritárias nos Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, visando a implementação de um sistema de monitoramento participativo da regeneração da vegetação natural, no âmbito do Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil – Fase 2).

 

O Beneficiário recebeu uma doação do Banco Mundial para a execução do Projeto PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA FASE 2 – ASL BRASIL 2 de n° TF0B6898. O Projeto tem como principal objetivo promover a gestão integrada da paisagem e a conservação de ecossistemas terrestres e de água doce em áreas específicas, a fim de melhorar o manejo e a conectividade de Áreas Protegidas na Região Amazônica.

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 0015/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, OU SIMPLESMENTE FGV, TORNA PÚBLICO QUE ESTÁ ABERTO O PRAZO PARA CONSULTORIAS ELEGÍVEIS INTERESSADAS NA APRESENTAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, COM VISTAS À CONTRATAÇÃO DE CONSULTORIA NÃO INDIVIDUAL (PESSOA JURÍDICA) ESPECIALIZADA EM MAPEAMENTO E DEFINIÇÃO DE ÁREAS PRIORITÁRIAS NOS Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, no município de Santarém, estado do Pará, visando subsidiar a implementação de um sistema de monitoramento participativo da regeneração da vegetação natural. As consultorias interessadas deverão demonstrar que são qualificadas e que têm a experiência para desempenhar o serviço, conforme descrito no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes

 

Qualificação Requerida da Consultoria

A consultoria deverá apresentar experiência em:

i.     Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) trabalhos concluídos nos últimos 10 (dez) anos, relacionados aos seguintes temas: identificação e mapeamento de áreas com aptidão para restauração florestal ou para regeneração da vegetação natural preferencialmente na Amazônia; implantação, fortalecimento e monitoramento de sistemas produtivos, sistemas agroflorestais, restauração de florestal, agricultura regenerativa, monitoramento da restauração na preferencialmente na Amazônia, mapeamento participativo em territórios quilombolas e outras comunidades tradicionais.

ii.     Execução de, no mínimo, 5 (cinco) contratos, projetos ou serviçosno desenvolvimento de, diagnósticos socioeconômicos e ambientais, desenvolvimento de sistemas agroflorestais, agricultura regenerativa, regeneração da vegetação nativa preferencialmente no estado do Pará e/ou em outras áreas com reconhecimento de gestão integrada na Amazônia.

iii.    Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) contratos, projetos ou serviços  de gestão ambiental e territorial com mapeamento participativo em áreas rurais de comunidades agricultoras, extrativistas, quilombolas ou indígenas, preferencialmente na Amazônia.

iv.   Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) contratos, projetos ou serviços de planejamento e monitoramento de políticas públicas socioambientais com elaboração de bases de dados, indicadores e sistemas de monitoramento da regeneração da vegetação, preferencialmente na Amazônia.

 

Será considerada diferencial a experiência comprovada na Amazônia Legal e, especialmente, no estado do Pará. A consultoria deverá demonstrar capacidade técnica para planejar e executar pesquisas de campo em múltiplos territórios; produzir análises socioeconômicas, ambientais e institucionais; operar ferramentas de georreferenciamento e sistemas de informação geográfica (SIG); elaborar bancos de dados e indicadores de monitoramento e produzir relatórios técnicos, mapas temáticos e documentos analíticos.

 

A equipe chave deverá contar com os seguintes profissionais:  1 Coordenador(a)-Geral e 1 Especialista em Gestão Territorial e Ambiental . A consultoria deverá designar equipe de apoio necessária para realização das atividades desse TDR, sendo sugerida a inclusão de um técnico para atuar em campo.

 

            As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 10/09/2026, às 23:59 horas, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. As Manifestações deverão estar identificadas como SMI Nº 0015/2026 – Mapeamento TQ Murumuru e Murumurutuba. A consultoria interessada deverá demonstrar capacidade técnica para atuar nos Territórios Quilombolas (TQ) Murumuru e TQ Murumurutuba, no município de Santarém/PA, garantindo que as atividades ocorram conforme o planejamento, que engloba o levantamento participativo de dados territoriais, o mapeamento e a priorização de áreas para regeneração da vegetação natural, e a proposição de um sistema de monitoramento participativo. A consultoria interessada deverá apresentar seu portfólio, os currículos da equipe-chave e demais documentos de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. As consultorias elegíveis serão avaliadas de acordo com as normas do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição de setembro de 2023".

 

Informações adicionais sobre o processo seletivo poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico asl2.compras@fgv.br bb

 

A Fundação Getúlio Vargas entrará em contato somente com as consultorias elegíveis para a próxima etapa do processo.

REVISED DRAFT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

MONGOLIA

GOBI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT PREPARATION (P514972)

 

GFPP Grant No.: TF0D0692

 

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Feasibility Study and Preliminary Design of Ulaanbaatar - Mandalgovi Road Reconstruction Project

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): ZTYa/20260804057

 

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), under Grant No. TF0D0692 to support the preparation of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project. The objective of the grant is to facilitate the preparation of a proposed project designed to enhance the efficiency, safety, and climate resilience of transport along the Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi road corridor, while strengthening institutional capacity for its sustainable maintenance.

 

The Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi (A0201) corridor is a nationally significant transport artery that forms a central spine in Mongolia’s north–south mobility network. Stretching approximately 272km, the corridor links Ulaanbaatar with the aimag centers of Tuv and Dundgobi while providing a gateway to southern regions with economies shaped by livestock, mining, tourism, and services. The road is also an important feeder into broader regional transport and trade corridors, including routes serving large scale mining operations and cross border freight movements.

 

Originally constructed in 2012–2013 to Asian Highway ClassIII standards, the existing two-lane road has reached a critical stage of deterioration. The corridor’s geometric design, originally intended for lower traffic volumes and slower heavy vehicle growth, no longer aligns with current or projected operational demands.

 

In response to these factors, the Ministry of Road and Transport (MRT) seeks a comprehensive feasibility assessment, including the preparation of preliminary design, that evaluates the potential of upgrading the A0201 corridor to a fourlane Class I standard. This upgrade would enhance freight fluidity, reduce travel times, strengthen supply chain reliability, and improve road safety outcomes. In line with the Government of Mongolia’s Action Plan for 2024–2028, which sets the objective of initiating the fourlane expansion of this corridor, the assessment and preliminary design will serve as the analytical backbone for subsequent safeguard instruments, procurement strategies, and engineering design stages, ensuring that the reconstruction approach is fit for purpose, fiscally prudent, and environmentally and socially responsible.

As a crosscutting requirement, the assignment will also encompass environmental and social due diligence tasks, including screening against the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standards (ESS1–ESS10), preparation of the Environmental and Social Management Plan (PESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the consulting services for feasibility study and preliminary design can be found at the following website.

 

Tender.gov.mn

The Ministry of Road and Transport now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

1. General Experience

Minimum 10 years of experience in preparing feasibility studies and preliminary/detailed engineering design of major road infrastructure projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration.

In addition, demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving the preparation of environmental and social safeguard instruments for World Bank-financed projects or projects financed by comparable multilateral development banks, including at a minimum one of the following: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), or Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP). Evidence should be provided in the firm's EoI.

 

2. Specific Experience in Similar Assignments

  • Proven experience in preparing feasibility studies and preliminary design of major road corridors during the last 5 years, with contract amount not less than USD 500,000 (five hundred thousand USD);
  • Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions (e.g., ADB, World Bank, JICA, EBRD, etc.) will be considered an advantage.
  • The consulting team must also include dedicated Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.

 

3. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” seventh edition dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09.00 to 17.00 (GMT+8) on Business Day.  

 

The assignment will be carried out in compliance with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines. ESF competency will be assessed during the subsequent Request for Proposals (RFP) stage as part of the technical evaluation.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail to zolbayar@ipiumrt.mn September 9, 2026, at 11 a.m. (GMT+8)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Country

Project

Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER)

Assignment Title

CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO ESTABLISH A FISHERIES DATA COLLECTION AND STORAGE FRAMEWORK FOR COASTAL FISHERIES MANAGEMENT IN FSM

FM-NORMA-539887-CS-CQS

CQS

 

The Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are for the assessment of existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps and the design of a recommended coastal fisheries data management framework for future implementation. The assignment will cover the four FSM States of Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae and is expected to take approximately 12 months.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development (DRD), in collaboration with State Fisheries Departments, NORMA , now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

1. Objective and Scope of the Assignment

The objective of the consultancy is to assess existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps, and to design a recommended data management framework for future implementation. The following areas are not within the scope of the assignment: 1) training, 2) conduct ecological field surveys, 3) build databases, 4) validate protocols, or and 5) produce management recommendations. These activities are intended to be undertaken under subsequent consultancies.

Stage

Main Activity

Expected Output / Focus

1

Desk Review and Data Inventory

Existing literature, research reports, available databases, catch and effort, landings, market, ecological data, and metadata catalogue.

2

Stakeholder Engagement

Fact-finding and prioritization with State fisheries departments, research institutions, and communities; information disaggregated by gender, age group, and fishing role where feasible.

3

Data Quality and Gap Assessment

Gap analysis and scoring matrix covering completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, accessibility, and dataset quality tiers.

4

Institutional Assessment

Review of data-related capacity, systems, workflows, reporting, responsibilities, and data-sharing mechanisms.

5

Recommended Data Collection Protocols

Recommended SOPs for catch, effort, market, and biological data collection aligned with SPC, WCPFC, and FAO ASFIS references.

6

Data Storage, Access, and Governance Framework

Recommended database architecture, hosting, backup, user permissions, ownership, interoperability, sustainability, and accessibility arrangements.

7

State-Specific Ecological Assessment TORs

Four separate procurement-ready TORs for Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae, based on data assessment outcomes.

8

Ecological Assessment Data Needs Prioritization

Prioritized sequence of future State ecological data collection assessments, including maps and GIS coordinates of priority sites.

9

Data Management Implementation Roadmap

Phased implementation roadmap with estimated costs, sequencing, and dependencies.

10

Other Subsequent Consultancy TORs

Procurement-ready TORs for data training and mentoring, protocol validation, database build-out/deployment, and data entry mobile applications.

11

Final Report and Presentation

Final consultancy report, handover package, and presentation of findings.

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Criterion

Indicative considerations

Suggested evidence

Relevant fisheries data management experience

Experience assessing and designing fisheries data systems, metadata catalogues, data quality frameworks, data gap assessments, and data governance arrangements.

Project descriptions, client references, outputs, dates, countries, and contract values.

Coastal fisheries and Pacific/small island context

Experience in coastal fisheries, community fisheries, ecological information needs, and Pacific Island or small island developing state contexts. FSM experience is preferred.

Examples of comparable assignments in Pacific Island countries or similar contexts.

Institutional and capacity assessment experience

Data standards and interoperability

GIS and spatial prioritization

TOR and implementation roadmap preparation

Examples of TORs, roadmaps, or investment plans.

Stakeholder engagement

4. Indicative Key Personnel

The firm should demonstrate that it can mobilize a qualified team. The TOR identifies the following indicative key personnel:

Key Personnel / Expertise

Description

Senior fisheries professional with expertise in data systems assessment and Pacific Island fisheries context. Minimum 10 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

Experience in data standards, metadata, gap analysis, QA/QC assessment, data-related capacity assessments, and institutional reviews of data systems. Minimum 10 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

GIS and Spatial Data Specialist

Experience in spatial data inventory, gap analysis, and prioritization mapping. Minimum 5 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

National Liaison Specialist

Knowledge of FSM institutions, fisheries sector, and stakeholder engagement. Minimum 5 years of experience.

Note: Detailed CVs are NOT required at this Stage. However, Firms may provide a brief staffing approach or indicate availability of the required expertise..

5. Selection Process, Associations, and Conflict of Interest

A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS)  procedures set out in the  World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment if selected.

Interested firms should provide information on any actual or potential conflict of interest arising from other assignments or conflicting involvement in related assignments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations on conflict of interest, eligibility, and fraud and corruption.

6. Submission Requirements

The Expression of Interest should include the following information, preferably not exceeding 15 pages excluding annexes]:

  • Firm profile, legal status, country of registration, and contact details;
  • Description of the firm’s core business and years in business;
  • Summary of no more than five relevant assignments completed during the last 5 years, including client, country, contract value, duration, and firm role;
  • Evidence of experience in fisheries data management, coastal fisheries, metadata catalogues, data gap assessments, data governance, GIS mapping, and institutional assessment;
  • Brief statement on experience in FSM, Pacific Island countries, or small island developing states;
  • Description of any proposed association, joint venture, or sub-consultancy arrangement;
  • Statement confirming availability and ability to mobilize for a 12-month assignment involving travel to all four FSM States;
  • Conflict of interest declaration.

APPENDIX C - Summary Terms of Reference for Publication

FSM currently lacks nationally standardized approaches for fisheries data collection, storage, access, and governance. Prior to implementation investments, FSM requires an assessment of existing datasets, information systems, institutional arrangements, and data/ecological information gaps. The FSM Coastal Fisheries SAR 2023 is the foundational reference for identifying priority data and ecological assessment needs across Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae.

The assignment will produce a data inventory and metadata catalogue, data quality and gap assessment with scoring matrix, institutional capacity assessment focused on data-related capacity, recommended standardized data collection protocols, recommended data storage/access/governance framework, ecological assessment data needs prioritization, four State-specific ecological data collection TORs, a phased data management implementation roadmap, and procurement-ready TORs for subsequent implementation consultancies.

The assignment is assessment and design focused. It excludes implementation training, ecological field surveys, database build-out, protocol validation, mobile application rollout, and management recommendations

Los Licitantes interesados podrán obtener el documento de licitación en español, previa presentación de una solicitud por escrito dirigida a la dirección que figura más abajo o al correo crep911@pronatel.gob.pe.

procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS DE DEMANDE DE COTATION OUVERTE

                                    Pour la fourniture de matériels et équipements de sécurité dans l’aéroport de                                                                   Toliara :01 machine traceur (marques de piste)

                                                                    (Processus à Une Enveloppe)

Pays     

: Madagascar

Maître d’Ouvrage

: Ministère des Transports et de la Météorologie (MTM) – Aéroports De Madagascar (ADEMA)

Projet   

: Projet de Transport Multimodal et de Logistique (PTML)

Financement

: Crédit A : IDA SUW 8005-MG, Crédit B : IDA 8004-MG

Titre du Marché                         

: Fourniture de matériels et équipements de sécurité dans l’aéroport de Toliara : 01 machine traceur (marques de piste)

 

DC N°                                       

: 17-ADEMA-F-PTML/2026

 

Date de lancement                      

: 19 Août 2026

 

 

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a sollicité un crédit de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet de Transport Multimodal et Logistique (PTML) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché de fourniture de matériels et équipements de sécurité dans l’aéroport de Toliara : 01 machine traceur (marques de piste).

 

2. L’Unité de Coordination de Projet PTML / Aéroports De Madagascar (ADEMA) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir deux (02) machines traceur (marques de piste). Le délai d’exécution est de CENT CINQ (105) jours après l’Ordre de service de commencer les prestations. L’inspection et l’essai seront réalisés au lieu de la destination finale (Aéroport de Toliara). La période de garantie sera de douze (12) mois après la livraison. Aucune marge de préférence n’est accordée dans le cadre de la présente Demande de Cotation.

 

3. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en utilisant un Appel de Cotations tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de FPI » septième édition, Septembre 2025.

 

4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de Projet de Transport Multimodale et de la Logistique (PTML), sis au Rez-de-Chaussée, Maison des projets, Enceinte Agence Routière à Alarobia, 101 Antananarivo et prendre connaissance de la Demande de Cotation durant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 16h00 à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

 

5. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un dossier de cotation complet en français en version électronique en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

 

6. Les cotations devront être soumises à l’adresse suivante Projet des Transports Multimodale et de la Logistique (PTML), Rez-de-Chaussée, Maison des projets, Enceinte Agence Routière à Alarobia 101 Antananarivo au plus tard le 30 octobre 2026 à 10h 00mn du matin. La soumission des cotations par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. NOUVELLE ÉCONOMIE DU CLIMAT

 

                  Unité de Coordination du Programme d’Investissement pour la Forêt « UC-PIF »

                                                      AMI N°ZR-PIF- 554591-CS-QCBS

Recrutement d’un Consultant (ONG) spécialisé dans les techniques améliorées de carbonisation dans les provinces du Kasaï et du Kasaï Central

 

N° d’identification du Projet : P178642

Date de publication               : 28 août 2026

Date de clôture                        : 17 septembre 2026

 

 

 
  

Contexte et justification

 

Cette sollicitation des Manifestations d’Intérêts fait suite à l’avis général de Passation des Marchés de ce projet publié dans le Développent Business du 4 septembre 2024.

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un crédit et un don de la Banque mondiale à travers l’IDA et les Fonds ESMAP, et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce Don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant « Recrutement d’un Consultant (ONG) spécialisé dans les techniques améliorées de carbonisation dans les provinces du Kasaï et du Kasaï Central ».

 

L’objectif principal de la mission « est de renforcer les potentialités des bénéficiaires sur les techniques de carbonisation améliorée. »

De manière spécifique, les tâches du Consultant incluront ce qui suit : Cfr TDR

  • La formation de 60 maîtres-charbonniers (20 par province) sur les techniques améliorées de carbonisation, chargés à leur tour de renforcer les capacités de 1 000 charbonniers chacun.
  • L’implication de 95 000 membres des communautés rurales, don’t 25 000 femmes et 17 500 jeunes, dans la filière bois-énergie.
  • La production et diffusion de guides pratiques en langues locales pour vulgariser les méthodes améliorées.
  • L’analyse et la mise en œuvre des chaînes de valeur du bois-énergie dans les provinces du Kasaï et du Kasaï Central.
  • L’organisation des charbonniers en coopératives ou autres regroupements économiques, et le renforcement de leurs compétences en commercialisation.

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) de ladite mission sont attachés à cet avis ou peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse ci-dessous :

N°78, Avenue de la Justice, Immeuble SKY VIEW 2, 6ème Niveau à Kinshasa/Gombe/RDC.

L’Unité de Coordination du Programme d’Investissement pour la Forêt (UC-PIF) invite les Consultants/ONG intéressés à présenter leur Manifestation d’intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les ONG doivent produire les informations sur leurs missions antérieures démontrant qu’ils ont la qualification et l’expérience pour les prestations susmentionnées.

 

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts telles que décrites dans les paragraphes 3.14 et suivants, du « Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) », daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé en novembre 2017, août 2018, novembre 2020 et Septembre 2023, sont applicables.

 

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres structures pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant.

 

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût « SFQC » telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir les Termes de référence et aussi des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous, aux heures suivantes d’ouverture de bureaux : de 9h00' à 15h30' (heures locales).

 

Les Manifestations d’intérêts doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 17 septembre 2026.

Unité de Coordination du Programme d’Investissement pour la Forêt (UC-PIF)

N°78, Avenue de la Justice, Immeuble SKY VIEW 2, 6ème Niveau à Kinshasa/Gombe/RDC

Tél : (+243) 984323214

procnotices.notice_text:
SOLICITAÇÃO DE COTAÇÕES Nº 001/2026

  1. DADOS GERAIS
    1. O Estado do Espírito Santo (“Mutuário”) recebeu financiamento do Banco Internacional de Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento – BIRD (o “Banco”) na forma de um empréstimo (denominado “empréstimo”) para custear o Programa de Apoio ao Fortalecimento da Gestão Pública do Espírito Santo – Programa Espírito Santo Mais Inteligente, conforme descrito no Acordo de Empréstimo nº 9679-BR.
    2. O Estado do Espírito Santo, por meio da Secretaria de Estado da Ciência, Tecnologia, Inovação e Educação Profissional, doravante denominada Contratante, por meio da Comissão Especial de Contratação do Programa Espírito Santo Mais Inteligente – BIRD, convida essa Empresa, doravante denominada Concorrente, para apresentar proposta, prestação de serviços de produção, sob demanda, de materiais institucionais de comunicação e divulgação das ações do Programa ES+Inteligente – conforme as Especificações Técnicas e anexos, com pagamentos por Preço global, de acordo com o que determina o item 6.7 da Seção VI e o item 5 do Anexo XII do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de IPF" do Banco, edição de setembro de 2023, e o § 3º do artigo 1º da Lei Federal nº 14.133/21 e as condições deste instrumento, doravante denominado SDC Nº 001/2026.
    3. As propostas poderão ser encaminhadas, até o dia às 23h59min do dia 10 de setembro de 2026, à Comissão Especial de Contratação do programa, por e-mail, através do endereço eletrônico esinteligente.cec@secti.es.gov.br. Não haverá sessão de Abertura Pública das Propostas.
    4. A Contratante fará a análise das propostas em local reservado, quando passarão a examinar a adequação das propostas enviadas aos requisitos estipulados no formulário padrão para apresentação de proposta (Modelo A).
    5. A proposta que apresentar o MENOR PREÇO GLOBAL, incluindo todos os impostos, e que estiver adequada aos requisitos, incluindo aqueles necessários à assinatura do contrato, será declarada vencedora.
    6. O nome da empresa vencedora e o valor ofertado serão publicados no Diário Oficial do Estado, sendo ainda notificadas as demais empresas que encaminharam proposta.
    7. Fazem parte desta Solicitação de Cotação:
      1. Especificação Técnica – Anexo I
      2. Carta de Apresentação de Proposta (Modelo A),
      3. Relação de Contratos Executados (Modelo B),
      4. Relação de Serviços do Responsável Técnico (Modelo C).
      5. Minuta de Contrato – (Modelo D).
    8. As despesas decorrentes do presente contrato correrão à conta da dotação orçamentária:

Programa de Trabalho: 10.32.101.19.572.0017.2366 – Universalização das

Tecnologias Digitais

Fonte de Recursos: 754 – Recursos de Operações de Crédito

Detalhamento da Fonte: 000114 – BIRD – Programa de Apoio ao Fortalecimento

da Gestão Pública – ES + Inteligente

Plano Orçamentário (PO): 002695 – ES + Inteligente

Natureza da Despesa (ND): 339032 - Material, bem ou serviço para distribuição gratuita.

 

  1. OBJETO:
    1. Contratação de empresa especializada na prestação de serviços de produção, sob demanda, de materiais institucionais de comunicação e divulgação das ações do Programa ES+Inteligente, compreendendo a produção de camisas, camisa polo, bonés, ecobags, canetas, squeezes, mouse pad, suporte de celular, pendrive e pin metálico, conforme as quantidades, características técnicas e condições constantes do Anexo I.

PRAZO PARA EXECUÇÃO: 24 (vinte e quatro) meses contados a partir da emissão da Ordem de Serviço.

PERÍODO DE VALIDADE DA PROPOSTA: 60 (sessenta) dias da data final estabelecida para apresentação da Proposta.

 

  1. PROPOSTA COMPLETA:
    1. A proposta deverá ser apresentada em papel timbrado da empresa, devidamente assinada por seu representante legal e será considerada completa e cobrirá a execução da totalidade do(s) serviço(s) previstos nas Especificações Técnicas.
    2. A Proposta deverá estar contida e ser apresentada pelo Concorrente, nos modelos-padrão a seguir:
  1. Modelo A – Carta de Apresentação da Proposta;
  2. Modelo B – Relação de Contratos executados; 
  3. Para fins de comprovação de qualificação técnica, será indispensável, juntamente com a proposta de preço, a apresentação dos seguintes documentos comprobatórios:
  • Relação de 2 contratos  ou atestados de capacidade técnica ,  que comprovem fornecimentos compatíveis em porte, complexidade e qualidade com os serviços ora contratados;
  • Catálogo de materiais que demonstre os procedimentos internos de controle de qualidade e rastreabilidade de materiais.

 

  1.  AVALIAÇÃO E JULGAMENTO DAS PROPOSTAS
    1. O Contratante avaliará as propostas por meio da Comissão Especial de Contratação, especialmente designada, da seguinte forma:
      1. se a proposta está devidamente identificada;
      2. se a proposta, de uma maneira geral, está substancialmente adequada aos termos e requisitos desta Solicitação de Cotações;
    2. A Proposta será considerada substancialmente adequada quando atender a todos os termos, condições e especificações contidos nas Especificações Técnicas e a qualificação exigida, sem qualquer ressalva ou desvio material. Ressalva ou desvio material é aquele que afeta de modo substancial o objeto, a qualidade ou o resultado dos serviço ou que limita, de modo conflitante com os termos deste instrumento, os direitos do Contratante ou as obrigações do Concorrente, na forma do Contrato, e cuja retificação prejudicaria a posição competitiva de outros Concorrentes que tenham apresentado propostas substancialmente adequadas.
    3. No caso de erros aritméticos (Preço Unitário x Quantidade), prevalecerá o Preço Unitário e será corrigido o Preço Total do item, sendo corrigido também o Preço Total da Proposta.
    4. Será declarado vencedor o Concorrente que apresentando proposta completa, tecnicamente correta e substancialmente adequada, tenham oferecido o menor preço global, bem como tenham preenchido as condições para assinatura de contrato.

 

  1. DA APRESENTAÇÃO DE AMOSTRAS
    1. Será exigida da Concorrente vencedora, como condição de adjudicação, a apresentação de amostras físicas dos produtos dos itens do grupo único descritos na Especificação Técnica que compõem a contratação da empresa especializada, que evidenciem o padrão técnico e o acabamento dos produtos; 
      1. As amostras deverão corresponder a produtos já produzidos para outros clientes, desde que sejam tecnicamente equivalentes aos itens especificados neste documento.
      2. As amostras deverão reproduzir, necessariamente, os mesmos padrões técnicos, materiais, processos de impressão, qualidade de acabamento e características construtivas, independentemente da arte gráfica ou identidade visual utilizada. Tais amostras terão caráter demonstrativo e servirão para comprovar capacidade técnica, precisão produtiva, domínio de processo industrial e conformidade com as especificações mínimas descritas nesta ET.
      3. Em caso de defeitos, divergências de especificação, falhas de produção ou danos decorrentes de manuseio inadequado, a Contratada deverá realizar a reimpressão ou substituição do material, sem ônus adicional à Administração, no prazo de até 48 horas, mantendo a conformidade com o padrão originalmente aprovado. 
      4. A exigência de material reciclado e certificações (como BPA Free) deve ser acompanhada da exigência de apresentação de Ficha Técnica do Fabricante no ato da entrega, sob pena de recusa do material. Normas Ambientais do Banco Mundial- BIRD
    2. A Contratada deverá manter, durante toda a execução contratual, o mesmo nível de qualidade demonstrado nas amostras e comprovações técnicas apresentadas, estando sujeita à inspeção, auditoria e monitoramento de desempenho pela Contratante e, quando aplicável, pelo Banco Mundial.

CONSULTANCY FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES - ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT

Loan No. 9017-JM

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (74104)

Reference No.: JM-JSIF-405452-CS-CQS

 

The Jamaica Social Investment Fund has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of : Consultancy Services for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”): Consultancy Services for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment.

 

Duration: 5 Months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for this assignment can be found at the following website: www.gojep.gov.jm.

 The JAMAICA SOCIAL INVESTMENT FUND now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that twihey have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The criteria are:

  • Demonstrable experience in conducting Environmental and Social Impact assessments of similar nature, scope and complexity (35 points)
  • Demonstrable experience in the assessment of the physical environments of large-scale waterfront developments that include coastal works, recreational and commercial buildings and other amenities (10 points)
  • Demonstrable experience in the assessment of socio-cultural environments of large-scale recreational developments that include Community demographic mapping and outreach, MSMEs mapping and support programmes, resettlement (15 points)
  • Demonstrable experience in the assessment of the impact of large-scale parks on a coastal area, community elements, programming and operations of public parks (10 points)
  • Demonstrable environmental engineering experience, large scale social data collection and measurement of air, water, soil and noise parameters involving government as well as private and civil entities (30 points)

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (July 2016 Revised February 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultancy Qualification method set out in the Procurement Regulations and to be set out in Request for Proposals. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

JOINT PROCUREMENT GRENADA & DOMINICA

Assignment: Outcome-Based Development of an Enhanced Lower-Secondary Curriculum and Assessment in Dominica and Grenada

Reference No.: GD-MOE-GRENADA-552260-CS-QBS
Project: WISTLE (P508559)

Grant No.: TF-C8594, TFC8596

 

Selection Method:  Selection shall follow the World Bank Procurement Regulations using the Quality-Based Selection (QBS) method.

1. Background

The Governments of the Commonwealth of Dominica and Grenada have received financing from the Global Partnership for Education through the World Bank for the Windward Islands Sector Transformation for Learning Enhancement (WISTLE) Project. The Ministries of Education intend to jointly procure a consulting firm to develop, pilot and support implementation of enhanced lower-secondary curricula and aligned assessment systems. The assignment will produce common regional solutions while contextualizing outputs for each country.

2. Objective

The consultancy will design and support implementation of an enhanced lower-secondary curriculum, strengthen national assessment systems, build institutional capacity, integrate digital delivery through an LMS, incorporate inclusive education and TVET pathways, and establish sustainable systems that remain after project completion.

3. Scope of Services

The selected consulting firm will: (i) review existing curricula and policies; (ii) develop curriculum frameworks and learning outcomes; (iii) prepare curricula, teacher guides and learning resources for Forms 1–3 in Dominica and Forms 1–2 in Grenada; (iv) develop a national assessment strategy, item bank and digital assessment library; (v) pilot and refine the curriculum; (vi) train curriculum developers, teachers and education officers; (vii) integrate resources into an existing regional LMS; and (viii) prepare sustainability and rollout plans.

4. Experience, Qualifications

The consulting firm shall demonstrate:

  • At least twelve (12) years' experience managing curriculum-reform projects, and at least twelve (12) years' experience in formative and summative assessment development, of comparable magnitude.
  • At least two (2) completed curriculum assignments and one (1) completed assessment assignment at basic/secondary level in the past five (5) years, the latter involving quality-assured items used in a large-scale assessment.
  • Graduate qualified team members in education, curriculum, or assessment, with proven research, statistical, and qualitative analysis skills.
  • Understanding of the Caribbean education context, with at least two (2) team members having demonstrated regional experience in the Caribbean or a small-island state; a local representative or partner in the Eastern Caribbean is required if the firm is not Caribbean-based.

5. Submission Requirements

Expressions of Interest shall include:

  1. Letter of interest;
  2. Company profile;
  3. Description of similar assignments;
  4. Evidence of technical and managerial capacity;
  5. Availability of key experts (Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage, CVs are not required at the EOI stage)
  6. Details of working in the region, specifically within Grenada and Dominica
  7. Contact information for client references.
  8. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

EOI’s should be a max of 10-15 pages.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered through electronic submission through the procurement system at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/Home. Candidates must register on this portal and submit all interest through this medium.

Upon receipt of the documents, a confirmation e-mail acknowledging the names of the files received will be sent.

Date for Submission: August 21st 2026, before 11:59pm Eastern Caribbean Time.

Further information can be obtained through In-Tend or via spo@procurement.gov.gd; or gilbertl@dominica.gov.dm  to seek clarification.

6. Shortlisting and Selection

Shortlisting will be based on the firm's general and specific experience, technical capability, regional experience, organizational capacity and successful completion of comparable assignments. The shortlist will comprise firms demonstrating the highest qualifications. The Request for Proposals will be issued to shortlisted firms.

7. Fraud and Corruption

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment i.e., 3.17 (c) & (d) of the Procurement Regulation.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:        SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON SYSTEMS OF NATIONAL ACCOUNTS (SNA 2025) AS A RESOURCE PERSON TOWARDS DEVELOPMENT OF A REPORT FOR THE REGION FOR MIGRATING TO SNA 2025. BW-SADC-563175-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/459

 

DATE OF ISSUE:              25th August 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services for Conduct a Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) as a Resource Person Towards Development of a Report for the Region for Migrating to SNA 2025, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultant to conduct Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  90 calendar days

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to harmonize national accounts statistics compilation and dissemination practices in the region to ensure Member States produce and disseminate such statistics responsive to data demands performing to regional integration.

 

  1. Specific objectives

The specific objective of the assignment is to service a regional workshop on SNA 2025 as a resource person in support towards development of harmonized national accounts statistics.

  1. Expected results

 

The consultancy is expected to achieve the following results:

  • Enhanced technical capacity of National Statistics Offices (NSOs) in SNA 2025 concepts, definitions and standards;
  • Action Plan for each Member State in a report evaluating the readiness of migrating to SNA 2025 in line with specific actions and timelines for future implementation;

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant with the specific profile as provided below:

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a master’s degree in statistics, economics or related field.

General Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of 20 years of experience in national accounts statistics subject matter at national and/or international level.

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrable experience in undertaking technical assistance as consultant in at least 10 assignments pertaining mainly to SNA 2008 implementation;
    • Demonstrated experience in undertaking technical assistance in rebasing of GDP in at least 3 assignments; and
    • Demonstrated experience as a resource person in at least 3 assignments in delivering regional training courses on national accounts to developing countries in Africa.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 90 calendar days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to venue of the workshop.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Tuesday, 8th September 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. No public opening will be heard.

 

 

SADC Collab Link: https://collab.sadc.int/s/62CCrrsgkEagt7Y

 

Kindly note that only highly technically scored bidder will be contacted for negotiations meeting.

 

  1. VALIDITY OF THE TECHINICAL PROPOSAL

Your Technical proposal should be valid for a period of 90 days from the date of deadline for submission.

procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Jamaica

Ministry of Labour & Social Security

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR INCREASED RESILIENCE AND OPPORTUNITY PROJECT (SPIRO)

Loan No.: 9652-JM

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

Name of Activity: Systems Analyst to Conduct an Assessment of Jamaica National Insurance Software System (JNISS) to Implement the Unemployment Insurance.

Reference No.: JM-MLSS-387381-CS-INDV

The Government of Jamaica/Ministry of Labour & Social Security has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Social Protection for Increased Resilience and Opportunity (SPIRO) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for an assessment of JNISS to implement the Unemployment Insurance.

Objective of the Consultancy:  The primary objective of this consultancy is to conduct a system needs assessment and gap analysis of the existing JNISS, and to develop a systems requirements document to guide the adaptation and upgrading of the system, as needed, for UI implementation, including its ability to capture, process, and report UI-related data.

Duration of the Consultancy:  The Consultant is expected to work for an estimated 90 business days over eight (8) months. If not located in Jamaica, the Consultant will be expected to travel to Jamaica to meet with stakeholders, gather information.

Selection Method: Individual Consultant Selection Method as set out in the Procurement Regulations. The evaluation will be based on academic, technical expertise and experience as detailed in the Terms of Reference.

Availability of the Documents: The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the consultancy will be available for download by Friday, on the following Government website: www.gojep.gov.jm

Submission Date & Time:  CVs must be submitted online via www.gojep.gov.jm on or before September 14, 2026, at 2:00 p.m.

To participate in the opportunity, the service provider must first be registered on the Government’s Electronic Procurement System at www.gojep.gov.jm.

For assistance with registration on the GOJEP portal, please contact the Ministry of Finance and the Public Service Help Desk at (876) 932-5220 or via email at opppcustomercare@mof.gov.jm.

For additional information about GOJEP, please send email to: mofprocure@mof.gov.jm.  

Contact Information:                       

Calesha Stewart Walker

Procurement Specialist

SPIRO Project

14 National Heroes Circle, Kingston 4, Jamaica

Tel: (876) 676-5819 or 876-474-3350

E-mail: calesha-stewart.walker@mlss.gov.jm

The Ministry of Labour & Social Security now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services for assessing the JNISS and developing a systems requirements document to guide the adaptation and upgrading of the system, as needed, for UI implementation, including its ability to capture, process, and report UI-related data. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
